configFields.name: condition_data_object_left
configFields.label: B: Data Object
configFields.sourceQuote: The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule. The administrator can create a condition based on:
configFields.notes: THE GATING COLUMN - it was the known miss in the prior build. The list contents are event-dependent (driven by the rule's trigger event), and the selection here determines what column C (Field/Value) offers. Ten values, each with a verbatim gloss in the corpus: 'Attendee Totals: An attendee audit rule based on the total amount spent on an attendee (by quarter or by year, for all employees or for the current employee)'; 'Budget: Budgets associated with an invoice or purchase request'; 'Detail: Detail-level fields'; 'Detail Allocation: An allocation'; 'Employee: Employee-level fields'; 'Line Item Attendee: A condition based on attendee information'; 'Request: Request-level fields'; 'Request Exception: Request exceptions'; 'Vendor Remittance: Vendor remittance fields'; 'Vendor Ship From: Vendor ship from fields'. WARNING for downstream consumers: Table 2 in this same file (the per-data-object field catalog) does NOT match this list - it adds Purchase Request, Purchase Request Distribution and Purchase Request Item, and renames 'Vendor Remittance' to 'Vendor Remittance Address' and 'Vendor Ship From' to 'Vendor Ship From Address'. Do not reconcile them silently; the corpus states both. Different-product copies of this same table list different objects (Print Condition Rules copy 3408dec8 lists 7; the Validation Rules copy the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md adds Field Validation) - those are out of Audit Rules scope.

configFields.name: condition_field_value_left
configFields.label: C: Field/Value
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list.
configFields.notes: Column C. Selection is made in a helper pane, not an inline list, and its contents are gated by column B (Data Object). The corpus points to the per-object catalog for the concrete choices: 'See Table 2.' Table 2 ('Table 2: Data objects and associated choices') in this same file enumerates the field choices for 13 data objects; it is a separate extraction target and is not reproduced here. Values are not enumerated in Table 1 itself, so validValues is empty.

configFields.name: condition_operator
configFields.label: D: Operator
configFields.sourceQuote: If you use the In or Not In operators for expense types, you can select multiple check boxes to include as many expense types as are required.
configFields.notes: Column D. Base description verbatim: 'Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon your previous choices.' The available operator list is NOT enumerated anywhere in this file - it varies by the data type of the field chosen in column C - so validValues is deliberately empty. OPERATOR SEMANTICS documented in this file: the In and Not In operators are multi-select for expense types ('you can select multiple check boxes to include as many expense types as are required'), i.e. the right-hand side becomes a check-box list rather than a single value. Further operator semantics documented elsewhere in the corpus are captured as separate entries below (Within date-range form; the Any/Every qualifier).

configFields.name: condition_data_object_right
configFields.label: E: Data Object
configFields.sourceQuote: The system provides the option that best suits the previous choices. Change it if necessary.
configFields.notes: Column E - the SECOND Data Object, on the right-hand side of the operator; a known miss in the prior build. It is system-defaulted, not blank: the system pre-selects the option best suiting the columns A-D choices, and the administrator may override it. Table 1 does not re-enumerate its choices for Audit Rules, so validValues is empty rather than copied from column B. Cross-scope datapoint (Invoice Processor, NOT Audit Rules): concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/the-query-builder-and-the-condition-editor-e10473f9.md says of the second Data Object 'This field will always display as Value and you cannot change this.' - that behaviour is stated for the Query Builder, and directly contradicts the Audit Rules 'Change it if necessary.', so it must not be carried into the Audit Rules model. The Validation Rules copy (the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md) uniquely adds List Validation to this column - also out of Audit Rules scope.

configFields.name: condition_field_value_right
configFields.label: F: Field/Value
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list.
configFields.notes: Column F - the right-hand Field/Value, gated by column E the way column C is gated by column B. Its description text is identical, word for word, to column C's, and it likewise carries the pointer 'See Table 2.' Constraint from concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md: 'If a second field is used in the condition, its data type must match that of the first field.' and 'A value is a constant and - like the field - can be of any data type. The data type of the value must match the data type of the field.'

configFields.name: condition_right_parenthesis
configFields.label: G: Right Parenthesis
configFields.sourceQuote: G: Right Parenthesis
configFields.notes: Column G - the mirror of column A, and a known miss in the prior build. Description verbatim, identical to column A: 'Select zero to three parentheses, depending on the complexity of the condition.' The corpus does not enumerate the individual entries, so validValues is empty. Pairing rule from concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md: the count of left parentheses must match the count of right parentheses, up to three per side; that file also gives three explicit examples of placements that are invalid despite a matching total count.

configFields.name: condition_and_or
configFields.label: H: And/Or
configFields.sourceQuote: Select either option to join the current condition to the next condition.
configFields.notes: Column H - the Boolean joiner between this condition row and the next. 'Select either option' plus the label 'H: And/Or' fixes the choice set at exactly two; corroborated in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md: 'When a conditional expression is composed of multiple conditions, each condition is separated by either and or or.' and 'It is composed of two conditions, separated by the Boolean separator of and.' Same file: there is no precedence of and over or - evaluation is strictly left to right unless parentheses (columns A and G) impose an order.

configFields.name: condition_operator_within_semantics
configFields.label: Within operator - documented date-range semantics (annotation on condition_operator; NOT a column)
configFields.sourceQuote: The Within operator defines a set of dates for the system to check against when evaluating the rule. For example, if you use Within Today -2 to evaluate the Request Submit Date, the system will look for the submit dates within the two ends of the range: Today, and two days earlier.
configFields.notes: SEMANTICS ONLY - annotation intended to be folded into condition_operator's notes, not rendered as its own control. It is NOT a ninth column and must not be shown alongside 'D: Operator'; fieldType is 'unknown' and validValues is empty because the corpus documents operator behaviour here, never a separate selectable control. PROVENANCE (explicit): the quote comes from the-condition-page-3408dec8.md, which is the PRINT CONDITION RULES copy of the shared Condition page ('The Condition page provides a user interface for defining logical conditions in Print Condition Rules'), NOT the Audit Rules copy the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md. Verified corpus-wide across BOTH the admin-guides and tools-guides directories: the string 'Within operator' occurs in exactly one file, 3408dec8; grep -cF 'Within' on the Audit Rules copy 5d4ea870 returns 0, so its column D documents only the In / Not In multi-select note and never Within. The cross-reference rests on 3408dec8's own sentence 'The Condition page in Print Condition Rules is similar to the Condition page used for Audit Rules and Invoice Processor.' - 'similar', not identical: the two copies demonstrably differ (3408dec8 column B lists 7 data objects, 5d4ea870 lists 10; 3408dec8 column A reads 'Up to three parentheses, depending on the complexity' vs 5d4ea870's 'Select zero to three parentheses, depending on the complexity of the condition.'). BEHAVIOUR: the operand takes an anchor plus a signed day offset, written as 'Within Today -2', and the range is evaluated inclusively across both ends ('within the two ends of the range: Today, and two days earlier'). Same column D in 3408dec8 also carries the In / Not In note plus the cross-reference 'Refer to Additional Samples of Custom Audits in this guide.', which the Audit Rules copy omits. Do not present Within as verified Audit Rules UI text.

configFields.name: condition_operator_any_every_qualifier
configFields.label: Any / Every multi-value qualifier - documented operator semantics (annotation on condition_operator; NOT a column)
configFields.sourceQuote: An operator is further defined by Any and Every depending on the type of data being compared.
configFields.notes: SEMANTICS ONLY - annotation intended to be folded into condition_operator's notes. fieldType 'unknown' and empty validValues are deliberate: the corpus never presents Any/Every as a selectable control on the Audit Rules Condition page. The Audit Rules Condition page table (the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md) has exactly eight rows, A-H, none of them Any/Every, and grep -cF 'Any' on that file returns 0. The quote is running prose inside a 'When creating or editing conditional expressions, consider the following:' bullet list, with no 'select' verb nearby. PROVENANCE (softened deliberately): understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md sits in the Concur Invoice Professional Edition Admin Guides deliverable but does not itself name Audit Rules - a case-insensitive grep for audit / workflow / processor / print condition in that file returns 0 hits - so it must NOT be called 'the Audit Rules copy'. The other half of the original claim does hold: 'further defined by Any and Every' occurs in exactly one file corpus-wide, sweeping both the admin-guides and tools-guides directories, so it is absent from understand-conditional-expressions-97cf41ea.md and from both tools-guides copies. GLOSSES (both verified verbatim in 9a165c46): 'ANY: Where a single expense of many associated with the report is true for the operator. As "the amount is greater than" for any expense causes the rule to be triggered' and 'EVERY: Where all expenses associated with the report are true for the operator. As "the amount is greater than" for every expense causes the rule to be triggered'. CAVEAT: the sole worked example is expressed in Concur Expense vocabulary - 'a Report Submit event combined with an Entry data object and Amount field/value' - and the glosses speak of 'expenses associated with the report'. There is no Entry data object in the Audit Rules Condition page's Table 1 data-object list. CORROBORATION, OUT OF SCOPE: the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md is the one place the corpus frames this as an administrator choice - 'the administrator must choose whether the condition will fire if Any or Every value matches' - but that is the Validation Rules Condition page, not Audit Rules. Applies when the column C field can resolve to multiple values for one parent record; it qualifies column D rather than being a column of its own.

configFields.name: and_or
configFields.label: H: And/Or
configFields.sourceQuote: Select either option to join the current condition to the next condition.
configFields.notes: Column H of the Audit Rules Condition editor: the Boolean connector joining one condition row to the next. Provenance re-anchored to the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md, the only file in the corpus that self-identifies as Audit Rules (verbatim: "The Condition page in Audit Rules is similar to the Condition page used for Workflow and Processor."); the column letter 'H: And/Or' is that file's own Table 1 row label. SECOND SOURCE (understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md — NOTE: that file never names Audit Rules; grep -ci 'audit' returns 0, so it is generic conditional-expression doctrine, not Audit-Rules-specific): the two connector values are enumerated there, verbatim: "When a conditional expression is composed of multiple conditions, each condition is separated by either and or or." EVALUATION ORDER (same second source, verbatim): "Parentheses are optional and are used to define the order of operation for the and/or operators. If the parentheses are omitted, and/or operations are carried out left to right. There is no precedence of and over or. The evaluation of the expression is simply left to right." NO CAP ON CONDITIONS (same second source, verbatim): "There is no limit to the number of conditions that comprise a total expression." Worked example there: "It is composed of two conditions, separated by the Boolean separator of and." DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: the Workflow-variant clause about the row appearing only between conditions (conditional-expressions-and-the-condition-page-4d98af34.md) — that file documents the Workflows tool's Condition page, not Audit Rules, and is not imported here.

configFields.name: left_parenthesis
configFields.label: A: Left Parenthesis
configFields.sourceQuote: Select zero to three parentheses, depending on the complexity of the condition.
configFields.notes: Column A of the Audit Rules Condition editor: the opening-parenthesis selector. fieldType 'dropdown' is corpus-supported rather than inferred — the Table 1 row describes it as a selection ('Select zero to three parentheses'). validValues is DELIBERATELY EMPTY: the corpus states a RANGE ('zero to three'), not an enumerated list of literal selectable values, so populating it would fabricate an enumeration (Rule 6). SECOND SOURCE — understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md (generic conditional-expression doctrine; that file never names Audit Rules, grep -ci 'audit' = 0). BALANCE + CEILING, verbatim from that second source: "If a conditional expression contains parentheses, the count of left parentheses must match the count of right parentheses. There can be up to three parentheses for both left and right sides." OPTIONAL / ORDER-OF-OPERATION ONLY, verbatim: "Parentheses are optional and are used to define the order of operation for the and/or operators. If the parentheses are omitted, and/or operations are carried out left to right. There is no precedence of and over or." PLACEMENT IS VALIDATED, NOT JUST COUNT — the second source gives one correct form, verbatim: "(Condition 1) and (Condition 2)", and three incorrect forms whose left/right totals still match, verbatim: "Condition1 ) And ( Condition2", "Condition1 ) And ( Condition2 ) Or ( Condition3", "( Condition1 )) And ( Condition2".

configFields.name: right_parenthesis
configFields.label: G: Right Parenthesis
configFields.sourceQuote: Select zero to three parentheses, depending on the complexity of the condition.
configFields.notes: Column G of the Audit Rules Condition editor: the closing-parenthesis selector. This is a genuinely DISTINCT control, not a mirror of column A invented for symmetry — Table 1 of the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md carries separate rows 'A: Left Parenthesis' and 'G: Right Parenthesis', each with its own description; the quoted sentence occurs twice in the file (grep -cF returns 2), once per row, and the quote above is the G row's own text. validValues DELIBERATELY EMPTY for the same reason as column A: 'zero to three' is a stated range, not an enumeration (Rule 6). SECOND SOURCE — understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md (generic; never names Audit Rules, grep -ci 'audit' = 0). BALANCE + CEILING, verbatim: "If a conditional expression contains parentheses, the count of left parentheses must match the count of right parentheses. There can be up to three parentheses for both left and right sides." — so the right count must equal the left count and the same maximum of three applies to this side. PLACEMENT, NOT ONLY COUNT, IS VALIDATED: that source's incorrect examples all have matching left/right totals yet are called out as wrong, e.g. verbatim "( Condition1 )) And ( Condition2".

configFields.name: operator
configFields.label: D: Operator
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon your previous choices.
configFields.notes: Column D of the Audit Rules Condition editor: the comparison-operator selector. The selectable set is gated by the administrator's previous choices (quote above) and is therefore not fixed. AUDIT-RULES-SPECIFIC CONSTRAINT from the same Table 1 row, verbatim: "If you use the In or Not In operators for expense types, you can select multiple check boxes to include as many expense types as are required." — i.e. the In / Not In operators turn the value side into a multi-select. validValues DELIBERATELY EMPTY: the only corpus enumeration is an open-ended example list ending in 'and so on', and the list is explicitly data-type dependent — second source understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md (generic; never names Audit Rules, grep -ci 'audit' = 0), verbatim: "An operator is one of several pre-defined comparison operators (equals, not equals, is greater than, and so on). The list of operators changes depending on the type of data being compared." Condition shape from the same second source, verbatim: "Most conditions are comprised of a field, then an operator, and then a value." ANY/EVERY — UNVERIFIED FOR CONCUR INVOICE AUDIT RULES, DO NOT TREAT AS CONFIRMED INVOICE BEHAVIOR: the second source states, verbatim, "An operator is further defined by Any and Every depending on the type of data being compared. For example, a Report Submit event combined with an Entry data object and Amount field/value results in an Operator value that can have multiple values and thus multiple interpretations.", with meanings verbatim "ANY: Where a single expense of many associated with the report is true for the operator. As \"the amount is greater than\" for any expense causes the rule to be triggered" and "EVERY: Where all expenses associated with the report are true for the operator. As \"the amount is greater than\" for every expense causes the rule to be triggered". That example turns on a 'Report Submit' event and an 'Entry' data object, and NEITHER exists in Invoice Audit Rules: add-a-custom-audit-rule-0f1d320e.md enumerates the events as Allocation Save, Payment Request Details Save, Payment Request Details Submit, Payment Request Save, Payment Request Submit, Payment Post Request Submit (grep -cF 'Report Submit' on that file returns 0), and Table 1 column B of the Audit Rules Condition page has no 'Entry' object. Any/Every is documented as a further definition OF the operator, with no column label of its own, so it is recorded here rather than promoted to a separate node.

configFields.name: data_object
configFields.label: B: Data Object
configFields.sourceQuote: The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule.
configFields.notes: Column B of the Audit Rules Condition editor: the left-hand data-object selector, and the GATING column of the whole row. Its own contents are gated upstream by the rule's trigger event (quote above); downstream it scopes what appears in column C Field/Value, and the field chosen there fixes the data type that the column D operator list and the comparison value must honour. validValues is taken verbatim and in corpus order from Table 1 column B ONLY, where each entry carries its own gloss: Attendee Totals ('An attendee audit rule based on the total amount spent on an attendee (by quarter or by year, for all employees or for the current employee)'), Budget ('Budgets associated with an invoice or purchase request'), Detail ('Detail-level fields'), Detail Allocation ('An allocation'), Employee ('Employee-level fields'), Line Item Attendee ('A condition based on attendee information'), Request ('Request-level fields'), Request Exception ('Request exceptions'), Vendor Remittance ('Vendor remittance fields'), Vendor Ship From ('Vendor ship from fields'). TABLE 2 DIVERGENCE — DO NOT MERGE: Table 2 on the same page ('Data objects and associated choices') is a per-object field catalog keyed by a DIFFERENT and LARGER object list. Its left-column headings are Attendee Totals, Budget, Detail, Detail Allocation, Employee, Line Item Attendee, Purchase Request, Purchase Request Distribution, Purchase Request Item, Request, Request Exception, Vendor Remittance Address, Vendor Ship From Address — i.e. it adds Purchase Request, Purchase Request Distribution and Purchase Request Item, and renames the two vendor objects with the suffix 'Address'. Merging Table 2's headings into this dropdown would fabricate the contents of the B list, so the divergence is recorded here instead. SECOND SOURCE — understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md (generic; never names Audit Rules, grep -ci 'audit' = 0) defines the object/field relationship in the abstract only and enumerates nothing, verbatim: "A field consists of a data object (essentially a database table) and fields in that data object (essentially a database column). The field selected defines the data type of the condition (number, text, date, and so on)."

configFields.name: field_value
configFields.label: C: Field/Value
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list.
configFields.notes: Column C of the Audit Rules Condition editor: the left-hand side of the comparison — a field of the selected data object, or a constant value. WIDGET: the corpus describes it as a HELPER PANE that appears and from which the administrator selects an item (quote above); 'dropdown' is the nearest supported schema value for that single-item picker, and the corpus's own wording is 'helper pane', not 'drop-down list'. GATING: the pane's contents are scoped by the selection made in column B (Data Object). validValues DELIBERATELY EMPTY — the selectable set varies per data object and is catalogued per object in Table 2 of this same file ('Table 2: Data objects and associated choices'), to which the C row itself cross-references, verbatim: "See Table 2." That catalog runs to roughly 250 field names across thirteen object headings; flattening it into this node's validValues would misrepresent a per-object catalog as one flat list, so the pointer is recorded here instead. SECOND SOURCE — understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md (generic; never names Audit Rules, grep -ci 'audit' = 0). DATA-TYPE CONSTRAINTS, verbatim: "A value is a constant and – like the field – can be of any data type. The data type of the value must match the data type of the field." and "The field selected defines the data type of the condition (number, text, date, and so on)."

configFields.name: second_field_value
configFields.label: F: Field/Value
configFields.sourceQuote: Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list.
configFields.notes: Column F of the Audit Rules Condition editor: the right-hand side of the comparison — an optional second field (or constant). This is a genuinely distinct control, not a duplicate of column C: Table 1 of the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md carries separate rows 'C: Field/Value' and 'F: Field/Value', and the quoted sentence occurs twice in the file (grep -cF returns 2), once per row. DEPENDENCY CORRECTION: F is scoped by the SECOND data-object selector, column E, NOT by column B. Column E's own Table 1 description is, verbatim: "The system provides the option that best suits the previous choices. Change it if necessary." — so the system pre-selects E from the preceding choices and the administrator may override it, and whatever E ends up holding is what drives F's helper pane. WIDGET: 'helper pane' from which an item is selected (quote above); 'dropdown' is the nearest supported schema value for that single-item picker, and 'helper pane' is the corpus's own wording. validValues DELIBERATELY EMPTY — the selectable set varies per data object and is catalogued per object in Table 2 of this same file, to which the F row itself cross-references, verbatim: "See Table 2." SECOND SOURCE — understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md (generic; never names Audit Rules, grep -ci 'audit' = 0). FIELD-TO-FIELD TYPE MATCH, verbatim: "If a second field is used in the condition, its data type must match that of the first field." Where a constant is used instead, the same matching rule applies, verbatim: "The data type of the value must match the data type of the field."

configFields.name: validation_condition_field_value_f
configFields.label: F: Field/Value
configFields.sourceQuote: Field Validation: This will display the list of columns from the validation table. Only columns that match the data type selected in field C above will display.
configFields.notes: CROSS-REFERENCE node. Right-hand Field/Value. Two documented behaviours: 'List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists.' and the Field Validation data-type filter quoted above — F is narrowed to columns whose data type matches the selection in C, which is the silent cause of an expected column not appearing. Governed also by the short-code lookup semantics in validation-conditional-expressions-67302876.md.

configFields.name: data_object_field_validation
configFields.label: Field Validation
configFields.sourceQuote: The Field Validation data object must be selected in order to use fields in the validation table for comparison.
configFields.notes: NOT A STANDALONE CONTROL — this is an enumerated OPTION of the column B Data Object dropdown (see validation_condition_data_object_b, where 'Field Validation' is already carried as a validValue). fieldType is 'unknown' only because the output schema offers no option/enum-member type; it is emphatically not an untyped input. VALUE-OF: validation_condition_data_object_b. SCOPE: Validation Rules only — verified by diff, the Audit Rules column B list in the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md enumerates Attendee Totals, Budget, Detail, Detail Allocation, Employee, Line Item Attendee, Request, Request Exception, Vendor Remittance, Vendor Ship From, and contains no Field Validation. CONSTRAINTS, all verbatim from this file: (1) 'Conditional expressions in Validation Rules are similar to creating database queries. Each condition using the Field Validation data object narrows down the list of potential matches. To match an invoice/entry item field with a field in the validation table, it is necessary to use multiple conditions to specify the correct validation table row.' (2) 'The Type and Id 01 fields must be included when using the Field Validation data object.' (3) 'The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator. This is the same for the Detail Allocation object.' (4) 'When using the Field Validation object the Id fields must all be used in numeric order 1 through n. For example, if you use Id 5 you must use Id 1 through Id 4 first.' ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE ONLY — the guide's worked example, its values are NOT enumerable and must never be read as validValues: 'The Account Code equals PMT validation table entry for Id 01 "Balance Sheet" AND Custom01 (Cost Center) on the allocation has a value entered (is not blank).' This file enumerates NO per-object field list for Field Validation; the pickable columns come from the client's own validation table (see validation_condition_field_value_c).

configFields.name: data_object_list_validation
configFields.label: List Validation
configFields.sourceQuote: When the List Validation object is selected, the List Validation Helper pane will appear on the right side of the page, displaying the configured simple lists.
configFields.notes: NOT A STANDALONE CONTROL — an enumerated OPTION of a Data Object list. fieldType 'unknown' only because the schema has no option/enum-member type. STRUCTURED CONSTRAINT — AVAILABILITY: column E ONLY, never column B. Corroborated verbatim in the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md line 102: 'List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists and is only available on the second data object selection list.' Diff confirms List Validation is absent from that page's column B enumeration. VALUE-OF: validation_condition_data_object_e. NOTE ALSO: the same page's F: Field/Value cell separately carries 'List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists.' (line 113), so the 'second data object selection list' restriction governs the Data Object lists (B vs E), not the F helper pane. Selecting it opens list_validation_helper_pane. validValues empty and non-enumerable — they are 'the configured simple lists' of the tenant. SHORT-CODE LOOKUP SEMANTICS, verbatim from this file: 'When looking up list values, the list item short code is used:' / 'When copying from one list to another, the source list short code for the current value is used to look up the short code in the target list.' / 'When copying from a text field, the text field value is compared to the short code value.' / 'When copying from a constant value that value is compared to the short code value.' Sweep of BOTH corpus directories: 'List Validation' occurs only at lines 102 and 113 of the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md and line 72 of this file.

configFields.name: list_validation_helper_pane
configFields.label: List Validation Helper
configFields.sourceQuote: the List Validation Helper pane will appear on the right side of the page, displaying the configured simple lists
configFields.notes: CLASSIFICATION: non-input conditional DISPLAY REGION (a selection pane), not a field and not a missing-type control. fieldType 'unknown' only because the output schema offers no display/pane classification; the corpus separately never states a control type for it. TRIGGER: selecting the List Validation data object — cross-link validation_condition_data_object_e. SUPPLIES: validation_condition_field_value_f, the column whose helper pane lists the simple lists. LOCATION: 'right side of the page', verbatim. CONTENTS: the tenant's configured simple lists, never enumerated in the corpus, hence validValues empty. UNRESOLVED BY THE CORPUS: nothing states whether this is a pane distinct from the generic C/F helper pane ('Select an item from the helper pane that appears.' in the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md) or that same F pane referred to by its proper name. Do not assume either. 'List Validation Helper' is a proper name the corpus itself assigns; it appears exactly once across both corpus directories.

configFields.name: data_object_detail_allocation_validation
configFields.label: Detail Allocation (Validation Rules scope)
configFields.sourceQuote: The Detail Allocation data object is used to validate invoice/line item fields against a list-type validation.
configFields.notes: NOT A STANDALONE CONTROL — an enumerated OPTION of the column B Data Object dropdown; fieldType 'unknown' only because the schema has no option/enum-member type. VALUE-OF: validation_condition_data_object_b, where it appears verbatim as 'Detail Allocation: To create a condition based on a Detail Allocation.' STRUCTURED CONSTRAINTS, SCOPE = VALIDATION RULES ONLY: (1) SIDE RESTRICTION — 'The Detail Allocation data object can only be on the right-hand side of the expression.' (2) OPERATOR RESTRICTION — 'The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator. This is the same for the Detail Allocation object.' SCOPE WARNING — DO NOT PROPAGATE: both restrictions are stated ONLY in this Validation Rules guide, which opens 'This section in this guide contains the Validation Rules variations.' The corpus does NOT state whether either restriction applies to the Detail Allocation object on the Audit Rules Condition page. CROSS-LINK, DO NOT MERGE: a separate Audit Rules Detail Allocation node exists — the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md carries 'Detail Allocation: An allocation' with its own Field/Value catalog in Table 2. The two are distinct nodes on distinct pages and must not be conflated.

configFields.name: validation_table_type_column
configFields.label: Type (validation table column)
configFields.sourceQuote: The Type field in the validation table allows the client to reuse columns for different data. The type field is just one of the values that appear in the validation table.
configFields.notes: CORPUS-VERBATIM DISPLAY NAME: 'Type'. The label has been qualified to '(validation table column)' purely to disambiguate; the string the UI shows is the bare word Type. DISAMBIGUATION — this is NOT any of the similarly named fields already enumerated in the Audit Rules Field/Value catalog: Budget Type, Period Type, Attendee Type, Tax Type, Pay Method Type, Purchase Type. It is a column of the client's validation table, reachable through column C/F when the Data Object is Field Validation ('Field Validation: This will display the list of columns from the validation table.'). fieldType 'unknown' — the corpus never states the control type. MANDATORY: 'The Type and Id 01 fields must be included when using the Field Validation data object.' OPERATOR RESTRICTION: 'The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator.' validValues empty and non-enumerable — the client reuses columns for different data, so no fixed value set exists.

configFields.name: validation_table_id_01
configFields.label: Id 01
configFields.sourceQuote: The Type and Id 01 fields must be included when using the Field Validation data object.
configFields.notes: MEMBER OF: validation_table_id_columns (the Id 01 – Id n column family of the validation table). Both family-level rules govern this node and must travel with it: (a) MANDATORY-WITH-TYPE — 'The Type and Id 01 fields must be included when using the Field Validation data object.' (b) NUMERIC-ORDER — 'When using the Field Validation object the Id fields must all be used in numeric order 1 through n. For example, if you use Id 5 you must use Id 1 through Id 4 first.' (c) OPERATOR — 'The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator.' Omitting Type or Id 01 breaks the rule silently. Referenced in expression syntax as 'Field\_validation.ID\_1' — the backslashes are literal in the corpus source; rendered it reads Field_validation.ID_1. Sweep of BOTH corpus directories: 'Id 01', 'Id columns' and the Field\_validation.ID\_1 pattern occur ONLY in validation-conditional-expressions-67302876.md, so there is no other source to reconcile against. fieldType 'unknown' — the corpus never states a control type.

configFields.name: validation_table_id_columns
configFields.label: Id 01 – Id n (validation table column family)
configFields.sourceQuote: When using the Field Validation object the Id fields must all be used in numeric order 1 through n. For example, if you use Id 5 you must use Id 1 through Id 4 first.
configFields.notes: THIS IS A COLUMN FAMILY / PATTERN NODE, NOT A SELECTABLE CONTROL. The corpus never shows a UI control labelled 'Id columns' — that is the guide's prose shorthand for the Id 01 through Id n columns of the validation table. Do not render it as a pickable field. MEMBERS: validation_table_id_01 and its numbered siblings. Two silent-failure constraints, verbatim: (1) the numeric-order rule quoted above — skipping an Id breaks the lookup; (2) 'The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator. This is the same for the Detail Allocation object.' UPPER BOUND: the corpus states NO upper bound on n. 'Id 5' appears only as an example, never as a limit — do not infer a maximum. Individual Id columns are picked through column C/F when the Data Object is Field Validation. fieldType 'unknown' — the corpus never states a control type. The numeric-order rule appears nowhere else in either corpus directory.

configFields.name: condition_operator_validation_scope
configFields.label: Operator restriction — Id columns, Type column, and Detail Allocation object (Validation Rules)
configFields.sourceQuote: The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator. This is the same for the Detail Allocation object.
configFields.notes: THIS IS A SCOPED CONSTRAINT, NOT A CONTROL AND NOT AN OPTION SET. It restricts which operator may be used against three specific operands — the Id columns, the Type column, and the Detail Allocation object — and the corpus expresses that restriction only in running prose as 'the equal operator'. NO UI OPTION LABEL IS GIVEN, so validValues is deliberately EMPTY: promoting 'equal' to a validValue would invent a label the corpus never provides (Locked Rules 5 and 6). ATTACHES TO: validation_table_type_column, validation_table_id_columns (and its member validation_table_id_01), and data_object_detail_allocation_validation. NOT THE COLUMN D OPERATOR CONTROL — that is a separate node, 'D: Operator' on both condition pages, whose full option set the corpus never enumerates: 'An Operator is one of several pre-defined comparison operators (equals, not equals, is greater than, etc.). The list of operators will change depending on the type of data being compared.' (understand-conditional-expressions-39d99456.md, tools guides; identical sentence in understand-conditional-expressions-db3d7418.md). The D column additionally carries the multi-value qualifier 'When a field with multiple values is selected, the administrator must choose whether the condition will fire if Any or Every value matches.' and an In / Not In note for Expense Types, both in the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md.

configFields.name: entry_city_validation
configFields.label: Entry City
configFields.sourceQuote: When using the Entry City field in validations, the location code for the city is used. You must import the location codes into the validation table to validate the city values.
configFields.notes: CLASSIFICATION: field-level VALIDATION SEMANTIC RULE, not a page control. PROVENANCE — named only in prose; not present in any enumerated Field/Value catalog in this corpus, and no Entry data object appears in column B on either condition page (the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md or the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md). Sweep of BOTH corpus directories for 'Entry City|Entry State|Entry Country' returns only lines 66, 68 and 70 of this one file. SEMANTICS: the comparison uses the city's location code, not its display text. PREREQUISITE: the location codes must be imported into the validation table or the validation cannot match. NO SIDE RESTRICTION is stated for Entry City — verified; unlike Entry State/Province, which is restricted to the right side. Do not infer one. fieldType 'unknown' and validValues empty — no control type and no value set are given.

configFields.name: entry_state_province_validation
configFields.label: Entry State/Province
configFields.sourceQuote: When using the Entry State/Province field in validations, the country sub code for the state/province is used. You must import the codes into the validation table to validate the State/Province values. Validation conditions using this field must have the validation on the left side of the condition, and the State/Province field on the right side: Field\_validation.ID\_1 = Entry.State/Province.
configFields.notes: CLASSIFICATION: field-level VALIDATION SEMANTIC RULE, not a page control. PROVENANCE — named only in prose; not present in any enumerated Field/Value catalog in this corpus, and no Entry data object appears in column B on either condition page. Sweep of BOTH corpus directories returns only line 68 of this file for 'Entry State'. THREE CONSTRAINTS in one bullet: (1) SEMANTICS — the comparison uses the country sub code, not the display value; (2) PREREQUISITE — the codes must be imported into the validation table first; (3) SIDE RESTRICTION — the validation must be on the LEFT and the State/Province field on the RIGHT, given in the corpus as the literal pattern 'Field\_validation.ID\_1 = Entry.State/Province.' The backslash-escaped underscores are literal in the corpus source; rendered it reads Field_validation.ID_1. CROSS-LINK — OPPOSING SIDE RULES: this left-side requirement is the mirror image of data_object_detail_allocation_validation, which states 'The Detail Allocation data object can only be on the right-hand side of the expression.' The two side rules must be read together. fieldType 'unknown' — no control type given.

configFields.name: entry_country_validation
configFields.label: Entry Country
configFields.sourceQuote: When using the Entry Country field in validations, the country code for the country is used. You must import the location country codes into the validation table to validate the country values.
configFields.notes: CLASSIFICATION: field-level VALIDATION SEMANTIC RULE, not a page control. PROVENANCE — named only in prose; not present in any enumerated Field/Value catalog in this corpus, and no Entry data object appears in column B on either condition page. Sweep of BOTH corpus directories returns exactly one hit, line 70 of this file. SEMANTICS: the comparison uses the country code rather than the country name. PREREQUISITE: the location country codes must be imported into the validation table first. NO SIDE RESTRICTION is stated for Entry Country — verified against the full file; do not infer one from the Entry State/Province rule. fieldType 'unknown' and validValues empty.

configFields.name: validation_condition_data_object_b
configFields.label: B: Data Object
configFields.sourceQuote: The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule:
configFields.notes: Left-hand Data Object list of the Validation Rules condition editor. The sourceQuote is the enumeration's lead-in, so it anchors the whole 8-member option set; the enumeration was verified COMPLETE against the file. GATING: the option set depends on the rule's triggering event. PER-VALUE EVIDENCE, verbatim glosses (note the CURLY apostrophe in the two vendor entries — a straight-apostrophe transcription FAILS grep -F against this file and must never be promoted to a sourceQuote): 'Detail: To create a condition based on Detail-level fields.' / 'Detail Allocation: To create a condition based on a Detail Allocation.' / 'Employee: To create a condition based on Employee-level fields.' / 'Field Validation: To create a condition based on evaluating an invoice field against an external field.' / 'Request: To create a condition based on invoice-level fields.' / 'Request Exception: To create a condition based on invoice exceptions.' / 'Vendor Remittance Address: To create a condition based on the vendor’s remittance address field.' / 'Vendor Ship From Address: To create a condition based on the vendor’s ship from address field.' List Validation is NOT in column B — it is column E only. DISTINCT FROM the Audit Rules column B list in the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md, which has a different membership (Attendee Totals, Budget, Detail, Detail Allocation, Employee, Line Item Attendee, Request, Request Exception, Vendor Remittance, Vendor Ship From) and shorter glosses; note Audit says 'Vendor Remittance' / 'Vendor Ship From' without 'Address'. Markdown pipe table in multi-line cell format; grep -c '<table' = 0.

configFields.name: validation_condition_data_object_e
configFields.label: E: Data Object
configFields.sourceQuote: List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists and is only available on the second data object selection list.
configFields.notes: Right-hand (second) Data Object list of the Validation Rules condition editor. RELATIONSHIP — this is the VALIDATION RULES VARIANT of the Audit Rules 'E: Data Object' column; the two are NOT the same node and must not be merged. I diffed them: the shared descriptive sentence is character-identical on both pages — 'The system provides the option that best suits the previous choices. Change it if necessary.' THE ONLY DELTA on the Validation Rules page is the appended List Validation bullet quoted above; that bullet does NOT exist on the Audit Rules page and must never be carried onto it. validValues left EMPTY deliberately — the corpus nowhere enumerates column E's full option set, and inventing one would violate Locked Rule 5. Only the List Validation addition is documented. Pairs with the constraint in validation-conditional-expressions-67302876.md that 'The Detail Allocation data object can only be on the right-hand side of the expression.' See also validation_condition_field_value_f, where List Validation is described again ('List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists.'), which is why the 'second data object selection list' wording scopes the restriction to the B/E Data Object lists rather than to the helper panes. Markdown pipe table; grep -c '<table' = 0.

configFields.name: validation_condition_field_value_c

configFields.name: custom_audit_rule_event
configFields.label: Event
configFields.sourceQuote: When creating or editing a custom audit rule, the administrator specifies the event that triggers the rule, for example:
configFields.notes:
DISPUTED LIST — the corpus contradicts itself and only the live UI settles it. validValues now carries EXACTLY the 17 values enumerated verbatim in the cited sourceFile; the bare string 'Allocation Save' was REMOVED because it does not occur anywhere in events-triggers-72339a13.md (grep -n 'Allocation Save' on that file returns a single line, the 'Payment Request Allocation Save' bullet). 'Allocation Save' is a Source A string only, and is preserved below as documentation, not as a value of this node.

SOURCE A (narrow, 6 values) — 'add-a-custom-audit-rule-43e3f9aa.md' (Legacy UI: 'On the Custom page, select New') and 'add-a-custom-audit-rule-0f1d320e.md' (New UI: 'On the Custom Rules page, select Create'). Both files carry a character-identical Event cell inside the step-2 field table, introduced verbatim as 'Select the event that triggers the rule:' — a closed-sounding phrasing with no hedge. Its six values: Allocation Save (annotated: 'Though this type of rule is triggered when the allocation is saved, the exception icon and message appear on the Processor List page or within the invoice. The message and icon do not appear on the Distribute Selected Items page.'), Payment Request Details Save, Payment Request Details Submit, Payment Request Save, Payment Request Submit, Payment Post Request Submit. Both files then point away from themselves: 'More Information: For a definition of each of the events, refer to the Events (Triggers) section in this guide.'

SOURCE B (broad, 17 values) — 'events-triggers-72339a13.md', the Events (Triggers) topic explicitly scoped to CUSTOM audit rules ('Event triggers define when custom audit rules are activated'). It is the very topic Source A defers to, yet it lists 17 bullets (recounted: exactly 17), adding eleven events Source A omits: Payment Request Attendee Submit, Payment Request Budget Submit, Payment Request Manual Assign, Payment Request Import Assign, Purchase Order Line Item Save, Purchase Order Save, Purchase Order Transmit, Purchase Request Distribution Save, Purchase Request Item Save, Purchase Request Save, Purchase Request Submit. Critically, Source B hedges: 'the administrator specifies the event that triggers the rule, for example:' — 'for example' means even 17 is not asserted as complete.

LABEL COLLISION: 'Allocation Save' (Source A) vs 'Payment Request Allocation Save' (Source B). Their annotations AGREE on the mechanism — the rule fires on allocation save while the exception icon and message surface on the processor list or within the invoice — but they are NOT the same text, and they name DIFFERENT suppressed pages: Source A ends 'The message and icon do not appear on the Distribute Selected Items page.' while Source B ends 'The message and icon do not appear on the Allocation page.' (both verified verbatim by grep -F). These are still almost certainly ONE control under two labels, since no other event in either list carries that mechanism; but the page-name divergence is a SECOND, independent point of documentation drift, on top of the 6-vs-17 divergence, and it is one more reason the live Event dropdown must be read for the tenant rather than trusted from either topic. Treat the true dropdown length as 17 (or 18 if the two labels really are separate options).

NET: 6 vs 17, with a 'for example' hedge on the larger list and a naming collision plus a page-name collision on top. DO NOT hard-code either list into a config. A config writer must read the live Event dropdown for the tenant's entity type — the Purchase Order / Purchase Request events in particular are plausibly gated on whether Purchasing is provisioned, though the corpus never says so.

SCOPE CONTRAST (these are separate controls, captured as their own nodes, and neither is contradicted): the VALIDATION rule Event field agrees on the value set and order across its two sources (12 values in both 'add-a-validation-rule-0b31c4c0.md' and 'events-triggers-7977f6ee.md'), and the RANDOM rule Event field agrees across three sources (2 values). Custom audit rules are the only one of the three where the corpus disagrees with itself on the value set.

configFields.name: validation_rule_event
configFields.label: Event
configFields.sourceQuote: Payment Request Distribution Save: This rule is triggered immediately after the distribution of the invoice line item information is saved whether by the employee, approver, or processor.
configFields.notes:
Captured as the CONTROL CASE for the custom-audit-rule contradiction, and it is not itself disputed. The Validation Rules Event field is a row in the step-2 field table of 'add-a-validation-rule-0b31c4c0.md' (introduced 'Select either:'), and the same 12 values appear in 'events-triggers-7977f6ee.md' (the Events (Triggers) topic scoped to validation rules).

SCOPE OF THE AGREEMENT, stated precisely: the two sources agree on the value SET and the value ORDER exactly, 12 for 12 — which is the property that matters for a config writer. Their per-event PROSE is NOT identical, so this is corroboration of the enumeration, not of the documentation. Two verified divergences: (a) Payment Request Allocation Save reads 'This rule is triggered when each invoice allocation is saved.' in add-a-validation-rule-0b31c4c0.md versus 'This rule is triggered when each payment request allocation is saved.' in events-triggers-7977f6ee.md; (b) Payment Post Request Submit is an unfinished editorial placeholder in 0b31c4c0.md only — the file literally contains 'Payment Post Request Submit: This rule is triggered <need information – what is this action?' — while events-triggers-7977f6ee.md supplies real text: 'Payment Post Request Submit: This rule is triggered after the invoice is submitted (only the Approver would see the exception).'

Even with that prose drift, the value set and order match one-for-one, which the custom-audit-rule pair does not (6 vs 17). So the custom-audit divergence remains a genuine documentation defect rather than a house style of listing only the common events.

Still hedged: 'events-triggers-7977f6ee.md' uses the same 'for example:' construction, so 12 is not asserted as exhaustive either.

NOTE the list is NOT a subset relationship with the custom list: validation uniquely includes Payment Request Distribution Save but omits Payment Request Attendee Submit, Payment Request Budget Submit, and every Purchase Order event (Line Item Save, Save, Transmit) that the custom list carries. The two rule types genuinely fire on different event sets.

configFields.label: B: Data Object
configFields.sourceQuote: The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule. The administrator can create a condition based on:
configFields.notes:
OWNERSHIP: this is column B of the eight-column condition editor (A: Left Parenthesis, B: Data Object, C: Field/Value, D: Operator, E: Data Object, F: Field/Value, G: Right Parenthesis, H: And/Or) documented in 'Table 1: Description of the Condition page' of the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md, reached from the custom-audit-rule wizard at 'Select Next. The Conditions step appears'. Emit ONE node under this name for the whole page, owned by the condition-editor set alongside A, C, D, E, F, G and H — do not duplicate it. It is retained here (rather than dropped by the events-triggers pass) because column B is the gate on the entire downstream condition vocabulary and deleting it before the condition-editor node is confirmed present would re-commit the exact miss this run exists to fix. If the condition-editor node already exists, merge this content into it rather than emitting a second node.

THE EVENT-TO-DATA-OBJECT MAPPING DOES NOT EXIST IN THE CORPUS — this absence is the finding. Table 1 states the dependency in one sentence ('The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule') and then never operationalises it. The ten values above are given as a flat, unconditioned list with per-object glosses; not one of them is annotated with which event exposes it, and no other topic supplies the mapping.

EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE, re-run this pass with BOTH directories searched at equal weight: (1) grep -rli 'based on the event' across admin-guides + tools-guides returns exactly four files — the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md, the-condition-page-3408dec8.md (Print Condition Rules), the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md, conditional-expressions-and-the-condition-page-4d98af34.md (Workflow) — and all four repeat the same bare sentence followed by an unconditioned object list; ZERO tools-guides files contain the phrase. (2) Nine files across both directories contain the string 'Data Object' (the four above plus create-reminder-rules-b0a7fac5.md, and in tools-guides managing-failed-check-payments-a08788a8.md, managing-recurring-invoices-a5f540ef.md, the-query-builder-and-the-condition-editor-e10473f9.md, the-query-builder-and-the-condition-editor-af058a80.md); NOT ONE of them also contains any event label (checked against Payment Request Submit, Payment Request Save, Payment Request Details Save, Payment Post Request Submit, Purchase Order Transmit) — zero hits. An event name and a data-object list never co-occur anywhere in the corpus. (3) Neither tools-guides query-builder catalog mentions events at all: grep -ci 'event' returns 0 on both e10473f9 and af058a80.

CONSEQUENCE for a config writer: the Event choice silently determines the entire downstream condition vocabulary — column B gates C (Field/Value), which gates D (Operator), which gates E/F ('The information that appears in this pane is based upon your previous choices') — and the corpus documents the cause and the possible effects but never which cause yields which effect. This is discoverable only empirically: pick an event in the live UI, then read the resulting Data Object list. It also means the disputed Event enumeration on custom_audit_rule_event cannot be validated by reverse-engineering from data objects; there is no bridge.

The three extras are exactly the Purchase Request family — which maps suggestively onto the Purchase Request events that 'events-triggers-72339a13.md' adds and the add-a-custom-audit-rule files omit. That is a plausible reading of both contradictions at once (a Purchasing-provisioned tenant gets the extra events AND the extra objects), but the corpus NEVER states it. Recorded as an INFERENCE TO TEST against the live UI, explicitly not as documented fact.
