configDependencies.condition: A workflow is built in Workflows and only afterwards associated to a policy. A workflow is inert until that association exists, and one workflow may serve several policies.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have created the workflow, you must associate it to a policy.

configDependencies.condition: Ordered: add the scan configuration in Image Handling first, then assign it on the policy. Cardinality is explicit - one configuration may serve many policies, but a policy accepts exactly one.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: To enable and configure this feature, you must first add a scan configuration. Once you have added a scan configuration, you must assign it to a policy. One configuration can be used by multiple policies; however, each policy can only use a single scan configuration.

configDependencies.condition: The imaging configuration must be created in Image Handling before it can be selected on the policy; the policy assignment is a separate, later step.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once an imaging configuration is set up for Concur Invoice, the client must assign it to a policy. This allows employees to utilize Imaging to submit invoices electronically. The View Image link will appear on the Payment Request page and is available to the Invoice Processor.

configDependencies.condition: Create the expense type in the Expense Types tool first; activation is then per-policy in the Policies tool. Creating it alone never makes it visible to employees.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have created a new expense type, you must activate that expense type for a particular policy for it to appear to the employee in Concur Invoice. You do this within the Policies tool.

configDependencies.condition: The print format must be created or modified on the Printed Invoices page first, then assigned and activated on the policy that will use it.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have modified or created a print format, you can assign it to a policy which will be used when users create invoices.

configDependencies.condition: An In Use rule set is frozen. Order is: copy it, edit the copy, then repoint the policy's PO Matching Ruleset at the copy. Alternatively strip all policy associations to unlock the original. Merged with the reverse-direction duplicate, which shared this identical quote.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: A rule set with an In Use status of Yes cannot be modified in any way. To update this rule set, use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed, then change the PO Matching Ruleset value in Policies to implement the new rules. Alternatively, remove all associations to the policy to allow configuration of the policy rule set selection.

configDependencies.condition: ADDED IN AUDIT. The billing address must be set up via Set a Default Shipping and Billing Address before the Bill To value exists to select, and the corpus states policy configuration cannot be completed until it is.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Refer to Setting a Default Shipping and Billing Address below to complete the billing address (as a minimum) so that policy configuration can be completed.

configDependencies.condition: Activating an expense type on a policy is gated on the Group Create right, not on reaching the page - an admin can open the list and still be unable to change Policy Status.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You must have Group Create rights to assign the expense types to a policy.

sourceRef.field: Invoice Configuration Administrator role and group administration rights to the Policies configuration object

configDependencies.condition: Two grants must land before anyone can create a policy at all. The topic names the Global Administrator as grantor but does not name the page the grants are made on, so the source page attribution is inferred from the role model, not quoted.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The administrator must complete two configuration steps before an employee is able to create policies.

configDependencies.condition: OUT-OF-BAND PREREQUISITE, not a control on any page. Timestamp Configuration is only configurable once the tenant-level e-Bunsho Timestamp feature for Japan is enabled; a crawler finding the field absent has not found the feature switched off, it has found an un-provisioned tenant.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When the e-Bunsho Timestamp feature for Japan is enabled, an Invoice Admin can configure policy groups that require group members to timestamp invoice images before the related invoice is submitted for approval.

configDependencies.condition: Policies must exist on the Policies page before they can be assigned to a group, and the assignment itself is performed in Group Configurations, never on Policies. Merged from two duplicate candidates drawn from this same file.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once you have created your policies, you must assign them to a group. Use Group Configurations in the Administration menu to complete the assignment.

configDependencies.condition: The Applies to column on Policies is read-only reporting of what was written in Group Configurations. Editing group scope from the Policies page is not possible, so a crawler must not treat this column as a control.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: actual assignment of the policy to a group occurs in the Group Configurations area

configDependencies.condition: ADDED IN AUDIT. The value rendered in the Policies page Applies to column is a function of Is Inheritable: with inheritance on it covers the named group plus every group beneath it, with inheritance off only the named group. The column is therefore not a literal list of assigned groups.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If inheritance applies, then the configuration applies to the group(s) listed in the Group column of the Group Configurations page, and all groups that are beneath the identified group, in the hierarchical structure.

configDependencies.condition: Two-phase: set Timestamp Configuration to Japan e-Bunsho on the policy first, then activate that e-Bunsho-enabled policy for the group. Merged from two duplicate candidates; kept the quote that actually states the ordering dependency rather than the procedure title.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In the Is Active for Group, check the box next to the e-Bunsho enabled policy.

configDependencies.condition: Rule 1 of 3 on this pair: a policy whose Is Active for Group box is cleared cannot be selected as the group default.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You will be unable to select a policy as a default if it is marked Inactive.

configDependencies.condition: Rule 2 of 3: when exactly one policy is Active for the group the system forces Is Default Policy to Yes and locks it. An auditor seeing Yes here has not necessarily seen a deliberate choice.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: if there is only one Active policy listed for a group, it will automatically be set to Yes in the Is Default Policy column. It cannot be changed to No until another policy available for the group is marked Active.

configDependencies.condition: Rule 3 of 3: once more than one policy is assigned to the group, naming a default becomes mandatory rather than optional. Source reframed from a non-field candidate ('Number of policies assigned to a group'); the quote says 'assigned to a group', and Is Active for Group is the control that performs that assignment.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If more than one policy is assigned to a group, then the administrator must specify one of the policies as the default policy (to be used if the employee does not select a policy).

targetRef.field: policy availability on a new invoice

configDependencies.condition: Marking the policy Active for the group is what puts it in reach of that group's members at invoice creation; Inactive removes it. Merged from two duplicate candidates.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If a policy is marked as Active, it is available for inclusion into an invoice created by a member of the selected group. If a policy is marked as Inactive, it is not available.

configDependencies.condition: Clearing Is Inheritable pushes child groups that have no configuration of their own PAST this group - they inherit from the level above instead. Merged from two duplicate candidates sharing this quote.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If a group below this group does not have a configuration associated with it, and this group configuration does not allow inheritance, then when an employee creates an invoice, it will inherit policies from the group above this group rather than from this group.

configDependencies.condition: Omitting a group configuration is itself a configuration decision - the undefined group silently inherits from the next defined level up. Absence of a row is not absence of policy.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If you do not define a group, then it will inherit from the next level that is defined. You always inherit the policy for undefined groups.

configDependencies.condition: Saving a new group configuration is not sufficient; the Policies (and Payment Types) columns must then be edited to declare which are active for that group.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: However, to create a new group, you must edit the policies and payment types to define which ones are active for that group.

configDependencies.condition: Reframed from a candidate that attributed the source to Audit Rules, which the quote does not name. A row flagged In Use is referenced elsewhere in the configuration, has no selection check box, and cannot be deleted until the referencing configuration is changed.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In Use is an indicator that a group configuration is directly referred to within the overall configuration, and therefore cannot be deleted until that related configuration is updated.

configDependencies.condition: Deleting a group configuration does not orphan its employees - they immediately fall back to the nearest ancestor group with a corresponding policy, up to the Global Group.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Once a group configuration is deleted, the employees contained within the deleted group will now inherit the policies of whatever group above has a corresponding policy in place, all the way up to the Global Group if required.

configDependencies.condition: Reframed to keep both endpoints on the audited page. Delete Selected Rows removes only the configuration, never the group - groups originate from the imported source list and must be removed there.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Although an Invoice Configuration administrator can delete a group configuration, they cannot delete the group itself.

sourceRef.field: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments

targetRef.field: CFDi Attachment command in the Actions menu

configDependencies.condition: Cleared by default. Enabling the group-level check box exposes the CFDi Attachment command to users in that group.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this setting (cleared/disabled by default) to allow users to view the CFDi Attachment command in the Actions menu and attach a digital invoice image to their invoice.

sourceRef.field: Allow users to upload CFDi attachments

targetRef.field: Attach CFDi and Delete CFDi menu commands

configDependencies.condition: Verification trap: even after the group setting is saved the commands do not render on an already-open invoice until the user saves and reopens it. Their absence is not proof the setting failed.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Users will not see the Attach CFDi and Delete CFDi menu commands until they have first saved and reopened their invoice.

sourceRef.field: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for

configDependencies.condition: The group-level per-role selector is what puts the Vendor Banking Information section on the Request New Vendor page at all.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: An option in the Group Configuration tool adds the Vendor Banking Information section to the Request New Vendor page.

sourceRef.field: Select whether vendor banking information is hidden, required, or optional for

configDependencies.condition: Value semantics, distinct from mere section presence: Required blocks submission for approval until banking data is entered; Optional leaves it discretionary; Hidden removes the section.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If visibility is set to Required, the Invoice Vendor Manager will be required to fill in some banking information before submitting a new vendor for approval.

targetRef.field: Payment Request Attendee Detail View form

configDependencies.condition: The per-group selection determines which Payment Request Attendee Detail View is rendered when a group member adds an attendee. LABEL DRIFT: this procedure calls the control the 'Forms Fields list', reached via Group Configurations > select group > Modify.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The selection that you have made determines which Attendee form that should be displayed when a new attendee is added.

sourceRef.field: Invoice Configuration administrator role group scope

configDependencies.condition: Which groups are visible and editable on Group Configurations is set outside the page, by the group(s) attached to the Invoice Configuration administrator role. Rights cascade downward only. Quote contains a U+2019 apostrophe in 'administrator's'.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The administrator’s group access rights are defined in User Permissions when assigning the Invoice Configuration administrator role. They will have rights for the group defined and any group below it.

sourceRef.field: Invoice Configuration administrator role group scope

configDependencies.condition: New group configurations can only be created for the administrator's own group and groups beneath it - never for peer or parent groups.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You can only create group configurations for groups for which you are assigned rights and for groups below those groups.

configDependencies.condition: The group is chosen first and the PO configuration is built against it, so the group configuration must already exist.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Each PO configuration you create is based on the Group you select before creating the configuration.

configDependencies.condition: Silent fallback distinct from the ordering rule above: a group left without its own PO configuration uses the Global Group configuration, so a missing configuration is not a missing behaviour.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Groups with no PO configuration assigned use the Global Group configuration by default.

configDependencies.condition: Hard cardinality: one Invoice delegate configuration per group. Broader coverage must come from hierarchy inheritance, not from additional configurations.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Each group within your company can only have one Invoice delegate configuration. However, through inheritance a configuration created for one group can be applied to all the groups below it in the hierarchy.

configDependencies.condition: Applies to the named vendor groups created on the Vendor Access tab. With no named group anywhere on the user's hierarchy path, the system does not restrict at all - the user sees every vendor at the Global level.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If no named group is defined in hierarchy path, then the user will have access to all vendors at the Global level.

sourceRef.field: source list levels and feature hierarchy

configDependencies.condition: Named vendor groups created on the Vendor Access tab must match the source list levels built in Step 1 and mapped to the feature hierarchy in Step 2 - the names are not free choice.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In this step you will create groups that match the source list levels you created in Step 1 and matched to the feature hierarchy in Step 2.

configDependencies.condition: Target retargeted to the field the quote literally names. The Vendor Access functionality does not appear in Group Configurations until Enable Vendor Segregation is set to Yes in Capture Processing Admin > Other Settings.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Now, the functionality appears in Group Configuration > Vendor Access

configDependencies.condition: Ordering comes from the numbered configuration sequence in this file: Step 3 creates the alias and its child email addresses in Capture Processing Admin > Email Administration, Step 4 assigns that alias to a vendor group on the Vendor Access tab.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Step 4: Using Group Configurations > Vendor Access, assign a vendor group its email alias.

sourceRef.field: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)

configDependencies.condition: Configure the duplicate-check fields on Invoice Settings FIRST, then create the Is Duplicate rule in Audit Rules. Setting the fields alone does nothing - duplicate detection never runs until the audit rule exists.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: After activating this feature, the admin must also create an Is Duplicate rule in the Audit Rules tool.

sourceRef.field: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)

configDependencies.condition: Direction corrected to match the graph convention (source controls target). If more than one field is selected on Invoice Settings, the Audit Rules rule must join them with an AND statement, or the multi-field selection is not honoured.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: To use more than one option, admins will need to use an AND statement when creating the Is Duplicate audit rule.

sourceRef.field: Default fields that regulate duplicate invoices (Vendor is selected by default)

configDependencies.condition: Firing is conjunctive, not disjunctive: every option selected on Invoice Settings must match before the exception is raised. Selecting MORE fields makes the rule fire LESS often - the opposite of the intuitive reading.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: All selected options must match for the audit rule to trigger

sourceRef.field: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information

configDependencies.condition: Enabled by default. Disabling it removes the Banking Import link AND all import/export functionality from the Invoice Payment Manager role, with no error shown - the link is simply absent.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If you disable the Allow Payment Manager to change banking information option, the Banking Import link and all the import and export functionality are no longer available for the Invoice Payment Manager role.

sourceRef.field: Allow Payment Manager to change banking information

configDependencies.condition: Distinct from the import-link effect: to force banking changes through the ERP / Vendor Master List instead of on-demand, the Invoice Processing Admin must clear this option first. The Payment Manager lockdown is the consequence, not a separate control.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Your company can turn off the ability to update banking details on-demand in Payment Manager. To do this, Invoice Processing Admins must clear (disable) the Allow Payment Manager to change banking information option in Invoice Settings.

sourceRef.field: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types

configDependencies.condition: Direction set so the Invoice Settings control is the source. No remittance email is ever sent unless this check box is selected; default is cleared in Professional Edition.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: For vendors to receive these emails, you must select the Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types option on the Invoice Settings page.

sourceRef.field: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types

configDependencies.condition: The setting only produces mail if the vendor record carries an address in the Vendor Contact field of the Approved Vendor Import; only one address is supported. Enabling the toggle against an empty Vendor Contact yields silence.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The email address for notifications is determined by what is entered in the Vendor Contact field of the Approved Vendor Import.

sourceRef.field: Send vendor payment email notifications for Check and ACH Concur Invoice Pay types

configDependencies.condition: Scope limit: the toggle only covers payments made through Invoice Pay. Client Pay payments never fire a notification however the setting is configured.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Payment of invoices that occur outside of Invoice Pay (Client Pay) do not trigger email notifications.

sourceRef.field: Peppol Integration feature activation by SAP Concur staff

configDependencies.condition: OUT-OF-BAND PREREQUISITE, not a control on this or any page - it is a support service request. The Enable Peppol Integration check box does not exist for the tenant until SAP Concur staff turn the feature on, so a crawler finding it absent has not found it disabled.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Peppol Integration feature for Concur Invoice must be enabled by SAP Concur staff. Clients must initiate a service request with SAP Concur support.

configDependencies.condition: The Invoice Settings check box (default cleared) only allows Peppol Integration; the actual field-level configuration is then done separately on the Peppol Configuration page.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box to allow Peppol Integration and configure the feature in Concur Invoice.

configDependencies.condition: Direction set so the Invoice Settings control is the source. CROSS-MODULE VALUE CONSTRAINT: once Peppol Integration is in use, Ledger Name on the Accounting Structure tab is pinned to the literal value 'Default'.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Customers using Peppol Integration must always set the Ledger Name as "Default".

sourceRef.field: Allow Invoice users to delete images on payment requests created on their behalf

targetRef.field: image deletion by the Invoice User

configDependencies.condition: Selected (enabled) by default. Clearing it denies the Invoice User role the ability to delete an image from an invoice that was created for them by the AP User.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Invoice Admin can deny the Invoice User role the ability to delete an image from an invoice created for them. By default, the user can delete the image.

sourceRef.field: Allow processor users to change vendor on requests pending processor roles

configDependencies.condition: Selected (enabled) by default. The restriction is workflow-state scoped, not blanket: clearing it blocks the Processor from changing the vendor only while the invoice is pending ANY Processor role in workflow.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select to allow a Processor to change the vendor associated with an invoice even during workflow steps pending a Processor. Clear (disable) to prevent the Processor from changing the vendor if the invoice is pending any Processor role in workflow (accounting review).

configDependencies.condition: Override layer 1: the site-wide default is a fallback only, applying to an invoice solely when no payment term is set on the vendor record.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: With the Default Payment Term (days) option in Concur Invoice, you can specify default payment terms, which are used any time individual payment terms are not specified on the vendor record.

targetRef.field: per-invoice or Invoice Pay payment term

configDependencies.condition: Override layer 2, distinct from the vendor-record layer: a term specified within the invoice itself or through Invoice Pay supersedes the Invoice Settings default. Default value is zero (0) days.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: This amount is the default for all invoices unless a different number of days is specified either within the invoice or through Invoice Pay.

sourceRef.field: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?

configDependencies.condition: Value = From the associated purchase order line (the default): PO allocation lines and their field values are copied to the matching invoice line automatically.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If clients select the From the associated purchase order line option, PO allocations lines will automatically be copied down from the PO line to the associated invoice line.

sourceRef.field: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?

configDependencies.condition: Value = From the copy-down configurations: this field defers entirely to the copydown configuration built in Forms and Fields, which then governs BOTH PO-based and non-PO-based invoices. Choosing this value with no copydown configuration in place produces no copy-down at all. Spelling drift: rendered 'From the copydown configurations' in one topic.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If clients select the From the copy-down configurations option, the copydown configuration of allocation fields will apply to both PO-based and non-PO based invoices.

sourceRef.field: For purchase order-based invoices, from where should the Invoice Line allocation be copied?

configDependencies.condition: PRECEDENCE, distinct from the deferral rule above. Set to From the associated purchase order line, this Invoice Settings value overrides the Forms and Fields copydown configuration for PO-based invoices - so a Forms and Fields change will appear to have no effect.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: With this setting, clients can copy down PO allocation lines regardless of the copydown configuration.

configDependencies.condition: On the hierarchy mapping import template, Employee ID is mandatory only when the Delete? column is not used; populating Delete? removes that requirement.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Required field only if the Delete? field is not used.

configDependencies.condition: Selecting the hierarchy path made up of the Level 1-10 Code segments causes the employee named in Employee ID on that imported row to be set as the default Invoice Owner.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The hierarchy path, in levels (segments) on selection of which will cause the associated user in Employee ID to be selected as the default Invoice owner when the AP user assigns the invoice.

configDependencies.condition: A source list must be specified on the Invoice Routing hierarchy in Feature Hierarchies before the hierarchy path segments imported as Level 1-10 Code on Routing Configuration can be mapped.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: A source list is required to map the hierarchy path segments for use.

configDependencies.condition: Auto-assigning an invoice by hierarchy mapping relies on the Routing Configuration import together with the List Management and Feature Hierarchy modules; the level segments cannot resolve without those lists in place.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: This feature relies on the Routing Configuration and associated import, List Management, and Feature Hierarchy modules of Concur Invoice.

targetRef.field: Custom field on the Verification form

configDependencies.condition: The Routing Configuration list of values mapped to Invoice Owners only produces straight-through auto-assignment when the corresponding Custom field (Store Number, etc.) is also included on the Verification form.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Routing Configuration feature allows clients to maintain a list of values mapped to Invoice Owners. When combining this feature with the inclusion of the relevant Custom field (Store Number, etc.) on the Verification form, an auto-assignment or "straight-through processing" affect can be achieved.

configDependencies.condition: Hierarchy mappings only exist to be searched on the Hierarchy Mapping List after the data has been imported from the Import Hierarchy Mappings tab.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Mappings appear in the Routing Configuration page after importing the data using options on the Import Hierarchy Mappings page.

configDependencies.condition: An exception must first be created on the Exceptions page before it is selectable as an existing exception on the Exception step of the Custom Audit Rule wizard.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: All exceptions created in the Exceptions page appear as options for the Audit Rules tool and Workflows tool when creating rules.

configDependencies.condition: An exception must first be created on the Exceptions page before it is selectable in the Exceptions window opened from a Random Audit Rule's Exception Code field.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: All exceptions created in the Exceptions page appear as options for the Audit Rules tool and Workflows tool when creating rules.

configDependencies.condition: Selecting an existing exception on the Exception step auto-populates the Exception Code, Exception Level, and Exception Text fields at the top of the page; Exception Level is not typed independently in that path.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: To use an existing exception, select the desired exception. It appears in the Exception Code, Exception Level, and Exception Text fields at the top of the page.

configDependencies.condition: A custom audit rule is an if/then statement: when the conditions built in the Condition Editor evaluate true, the exception assigned on the Exception step is created.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Custom audit rules are if/then statements. If the defined conditions are met, then an exception is created.

targetRef.field: Prevent this payment request submission when exception level exceeds X

configDependencies.condition: When the level on the exception raised by the rule is at or above the number configured in this Invoice Settings threshold, the employee is blocked from submitting the invoice.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Any invoice that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the employee from submitting the invoice. The employee must then make the necessary changes before being able to submit the invoice.

targetRef.field: Prevent purchase request submission when exception level exceeds X

configDependencies.condition: When the level on the exception raised against a purchase request is at or above this configured threshold, the employee is blocked from submitting the PR.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Any purchase request that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the employee from submitting the PR.

targetRef.field: Prevent purchase order transmission when exception level exceeds X

configDependencies.condition: When the level on the exception raised against a purchase order is at or above this configured threshold, the PO is blocked from being transmitted to the vendor once created from its purchase request.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Any purchase order that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the PO from being transmitted once it is created from its associated purchase request (PR).

configDependencies.condition: The exception level number assigned on a rule has no blocking effect on its own; whether that level actually prevents submission is decided by a separate workflow setting.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: A workflow setting exists that prevents an invoice from being submitted if it has an exception of a certain level.

configDependencies.condition: Submission blocking via exception level is available only on Custom audit rules; a rule defined on the Random tab (Percentage or Sequential) can never block submission no matter what level is assigned.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Custom audit rules can be configured to prevent invoice submission. Random audit rules cannot.

configDependencies.condition: With Event set to Payment Request Submit, any exception the custom rule generates above the configured exception level limit stops the invoice from being submitted and from entering the first workflow step.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Payment Request Submit: The rule is triggered when the invoice is submitted. If there are exceptions generated that are above the exception level limit (that is, prevents invoice submission; described in Exceptions in this guide), then the invoice will not be submitted and will not enter the first step of a workflow.

configDependencies.condition: With a validation rule's Event set to Payment Request Submit, exceptions generated above the exception level limit stop the invoice from being submitted and from entering the first workflow step.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Payment Request Submit: The rule is triggered when the invoice is submitted. If there are exceptions generated that are above the exception level limit (that is, prevents invoice submission; described in Exceptions in this guide), then the invoice will not be submitted and will not enter the first step of a workflow.

configDependencies.condition: The set of comparison operators offered in column D of the Condition Editor changes according to the data type of the field selected in the Field/Value column.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: An operator is one of several pre-defined comparison operators (equals, not equals, is greater than, and so on). The list of operators changes depending on the type of data the system is comparing.

configDependencies.condition: When a condition compares two fields rather than a field against a constant, the second Field/Value selection (column F) must be of the same data type as the first (column C).
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If the condition uses a second field, its data type must match that of the first field.

configDependencies.condition: The Data Object list in the Condition Editor (columns B and E), which in turn determines what the Field/Value helper pane offers, is populated from the event that triggers the rule; changing Event changes the selectable condition fields.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule:

configDependencies.condition: The event a rule actually fires on is widened by its condition contents: a rule set to Payment Request Details Save also fires at Payment Request Save whenever its condition references a request field.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If a rule that is triggered at Payment Request Details Save contains a request field in its condition, then the rule is also triggered at Payment Request Save.

configDependencies.condition: The Validation tab (and therefore every validation rule field on it) only appears on the Audit Rules page once the Enable Validation Rules site setting is turned on.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In addition, the Enable Validation Rules setting must be enabled for the tab to appear.

configDependencies.condition: The list of fields offered in From Field Name on the validation rule Actions page is filtered by the From Data Source selection.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The field from the Data Source that will be used to update the Invoice field. The list of fields displayed will change depending on the Data Source selected.

configDependencies.condition: The list of fields offered in To Field Name on the validation rule Actions page is filtered by the To Data Source selection.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Concur Invoice field that will be updated. The list of fields displayed will change depending on the Data Source selected.

configDependencies.condition: Which sources (Constant, Validation Table, Employee, Request) are offered in From Data Source changes according to the event selected for the validation rule.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The source of the fields that will be used for the update. The available sources will change depending on the event selected.

configDependencies.condition: The options offered in To Data Source change according to the event type selected for the rule.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: NOTE: The options available will change depending on the event type selected for the audit rule.

configDependencies.condition: Only one random audit rule should be active per group configuration; activating a second random rule scoped to the same Applies To group configuration is permitted by the system but produces unreliable selection.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Your company should have only one active random audit rule for each group configuration. The system may let you activate more than one random rule, but the results will be unreliable.

configDependencies.condition: The scope of a rule's Applies To selection resolves against the group hierarchy built on the Group Configurations page; with Inherited, the rule also covers every group beneath the selected group.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If inheritance applies, then the configuration applies to the group(s) listed in the Group column of the Group Configurations page, and all groups that are beneath the identified group, in the hierarchical structure.

configDependencies.condition: The groups selectable in Editable By are limited by the administrator's own position in the group hierarchy: only their own group and groups beneath it, never the Global group unless they administer it.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Depending on your rights, you may not be able to select the Global group. This means you are only allowed to select your group or groups that fall below your group in the hierarchy.

configDependencies.condition: Whether Remove is usable on an exception row is gated by the Editable By Group(s) value set on that exception; administrators at lower hierarchy levels can only copy it, not delete it.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If you select Global Group, then the exception can be edited or deleted by any employee assigned to administer the Global Group. All other administrators assigned at lower levels in the hierarchy can copy this exception, but not edit or delete it.

configDependencies.condition: Editable By Group(s) defines the group rights an administrator must hold to modify the exception; without them the Modify window opens read-only.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select the group rights that an administrator must have in order to modify this exception.

configDependencies.condition: The groups offered in Editable By Group(s) are constrained by the administrator's own place in the group hierarchy defined in Group Configurations: only groups beneath them, and Global Group only if they administer it.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Depending on your rights, you may not be able to select Global Group. You are only allowed to select groups beneath you.

targetRef.field: Verification and Document Separation task definition options

configDependencies.condition: the Client Managed Verification option for the Task Processor field must be selected first, or the admin will not see either the Verification or Document Separation options at all
configDependencies.sourceQuote: It is critical that these settings be configured prior to use. For example, the Client Managed Verification option for the Task Processor field must be selected, or the admin will not see either the Verification or Document Separation options.

configDependencies.condition: when Instruction Text is populated, the configured text appears under Instructions on the Verification tab
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When populated, the text appears under Instructions in the Verification tab.

targetRef.page: Capture Processing > Verification tab (Invoice Details section)

configDependencies.condition: setting Capture Attention To to Yes adds the optional Assign Invoice To field to the Invoice Details section of the Verification tab
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Capture Attention To option adds the optional Assign Invoice To field to the Invoice Details section of the Verification tab, which is useful whenever you need to manually search for and assign the invoice to the invoice owner or let Concur Invoice assign a vendor owner automatically.

sourceRef.field: Assign Invoice To (auto-population with Vendor Owner)

targetRef.page: Capture Processing Admin; Vendor Manager > Vendor Mapping List
targetRef.field: capture_attention_to AND Vendor Mapping List employee-to-vendor mapping

configDependencies.condition: auto-population occurs only when BOTH the Capture Attention To feature in Task Definitions is configured AND the employee is mapped to the vendor on Vendor Manager > Vendor Mapping List
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Assign Invoice To field is automatically populated with a Vendor Owner name if the Vendor Manager has configured both the Capture Attention To feature in Task Definitions, and the mapping of employee to vendor using options in the Vendor Manager > Vendor Mapping List page.

configDependencies.condition: if the client uses Routing Configuration auto-routing, Capture Attention To is not required and should be disabled (No); Routing Configuration takes precedence
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If the client is using the auto-routing features available using the Routing Configuration tool, the Capture Attention To option is not required and in fact should be disabled (No). The Routing Configuration takes precedence, and when enabled is usually considered the more accurate and easily maintainable assignment option.

configDependencies.condition: to switch from manual to automated separation, Document Separation must be set to Yes (disabled) in conjunction with setting Automated Document Separation to No (enabled) — the two task definitions must be changed together so exactly one separation method is active
configDependencies.sourceQuote: select Yes (disabled) in conjunction with selecting No in the Automated Document Separation definition to have the system perform automated (not manual) separation of document pages to processing-ready state.

targetRef.page: Capture Processing Admin > Forms and Fields tab

configDependencies.condition: the Header, Line Item and Vendor forms selectable in the Verification task definition draw their fields from what is configured on the Forms and Fields tab
configDependencies.sourceQuote: NOTE: Fields for these forms are configured using options in the Forms and Fields tab.

sourceRef.field: Invoice Admin > Forms and Fields tool field configuration

targetRef.page: Capture Processing Admin > Forms and Fields tab
targetRef.field: fields available on the Capture Processing forms

configDependencies.condition: fields are created in the Invoice Admin Forms and Fields tool, NOT on the Capture Processing Forms and Fields tab; they flow one-way into Capture Processing where only limited fine-tuning (e.g. renaming, Client-Managed Capture Verifier access rights) is available
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Fields are configured using the Invoice Admin > Forms and Fields tool (that is, not using options on the Forms and Fields tab in Capture Processing). Fields configured using the Concur Invoice tool are made available "one-way" to the Capture Processing forms and fields module for additions to that feature’s forms.

sourceRef.page: Capture Processing Admin > Forms and Fields tab
sourceRef.field: Custom field value on a captured invoice

configDependencies.condition: a Custom field is configured in the Routing Configuration tool so that, dependent on its value, the invoice is routed (assigned) to the correct owner's invoice queue without user intervention
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Using the Invoice Routing Configuration tool, a Custom field is configured so that, dependent on value, the invoice is routed (assigned) to the correct owner’s invoice queue.

targetRef.field: add_email_capture_type / capture type assignment options on batches

configDependencies.condition: when Dual Support is enabled, additional options appear that let the admin assign a capture type to one or more batches
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Dual Support lets a client process their emailed or uploaded batches using either capture method. When this feature is enabled, additional options appear that let the admin assign a capture type to one or more batches.

sourceRef.field: SAP Concur activation of Dual Support

configDependencies.condition: the client must contact SAP Concur to activate Dual Support (possibly for a fee) before the capture-type options exist; absence of the field means the feature is not activated
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Clients will need to contact SAP Concur to activate this feature. There may be a fee for this service.

configDependencies.condition: the alias-level None (Latin-based) OCR language setting is superseded whenever a language is configured in the Content Extraction task's Modify Task Definition > Default Language
configDependencies.sourceQuote: NOTE: The None setting is superseded if a language is configured in Modify Task Definition \> Default Language.

sourceRef.field: add_email_address (first batch sent to the address)

targetRef.field: email address visibility on the Email Administration tab

configDependencies.condition: a minimum of one batch must be sent to the newly configured address before that address is exposed in the Email Administration tab
configDependencies.sourceQuote: WARNING At this time, send a minimum of one batch to the email address configured for the client to expose the email address in the Email Administration tab of the Capture Processing Admin tool.

configDependencies.condition: a user can supersede the batch-level owner assignment at the invoice level only if the Capture Attention To feature has been activated for Capture Processing
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The user can supersede any assignment at the Batch level by assigning or changing the owner. The Capture Attention To feature must be activated for Capture Processing for this to work.

targetRef.field: Assign Invoice to Purchase Request Owner

configDependencies.condition: Routing Configuration's assignment (priority 2 in the ownership order) is only used if the Purchase Request Owner set in Invoice Settings is either not activated or not found
configDependencies.sourceQuote: User defined and only used if the Purchase Request Owner is either not activated or not found

targetRef.field: Assign Invoice to Purchase Request Owner (Invoice Settings) and Routing Configuration assignment

configDependencies.condition: routing an emailed invoice to its sender via the email alias (priority 3) takes effect only if the higher-priority Purchase Request Owner and Routing Configuration steps are not activated
configDependencies.sourceQuote: User defined and takes effect if the steps detailed above are not activated

configDependencies.condition: when an email alias has Owner Assignment set to Sender, all emails associated with that alias are routed directly to the sender, identified from the From address
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Create an email alias and set the Owner Assignment to "Sender", all emails associated with the alias are routed directly to the sender.

sourceRef.field: system-detected PO Number on a captured invoice

configDependencies.condition: if the system detects a PO number on the invoice, it changes that invoice's policy to a PO policy
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Conversely, if the system detects a PO number, it will change to a PO policy for that invoice.

configDependencies.condition: when a PO policy is invoked, the PO Number field becomes a Required field type
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Note that, if a PO policy is invoked, the PO Number field is a Required field type as this number is essential to processing a purchase order.

configDependencies.condition: the default policy set per sending method (upload vs. email) populates the Policy field for those batches on the Verification page, and the batch inherits that policy's attributes
configDependencies.sourceQuote: By setting the policy here, that same policy will populate the Policy field for emailed and uploaded batches in the Verification page.

sourceRef.field: unprocessable supplier email (unsupported document type; credit memos)

configDependencies.condition: when the system cannot process an incoming email, the original email is converted to a single PDF and attached to an exception notification sent to the address in Exception Email Address
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When the system encounters an email that cannot be processed (unsupported document type; credit memos), the original email is formatted into a single PDF document that is sent as an attachment in the exception email notification to the recipient specified in Exception Email Address.

sourceRef.field: vendors available during OCR and manual vendor change

configDependencies.condition: associating email addresses to a single email alias and assigning that alias to a group of vendors restricts the vendors available during the OCR step and when changing vendors manually during verification; a default policy and language attribute may be set the same way
configDependencies.sourceQuote: By associating email addresses to a single email alias, and then assigning the alias to a group of vendors, only those vendors are available during the OCR step, and when changing vendors manually during the verification step.

sourceRef.field: list of available vendors (Vendor Information, Verifier)

configDependencies.condition: when the Vendor Segregation feature is enabled, the vendor list the Verifier can choose from is limited to the vendors associated with the receiving email address
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If the Vendor Segregation feature is enabled, the list of available vendors will be limited to those associated with the email address as per the feature.

sourceRef.field: vendor search criteria available to the Verifier

targetRef.field: banking information entry status (Hidden; Required; Optional) by role

configDependencies.condition: the search criteria available when filtering the vendor master list depend on the Hidden/Required/Optional status applied to banking-information entry for the role, which is set with the Group Configurations tool
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Be aware that the available search criteria is dependent on the status (Hidden; Required; Optional) applied to the entry of banking information by roles using the Group Configurations tool.

configDependencies.condition: the Exclude from Capture option is only available to companies using Capture Processing and does not appear unless SAP Concur staff have enabled the feature
configDependencies.sourceQuote: This option is only available to companies using Capture Processing and does not appear if SAP Concur staff have not enabled this feature.

sourceRef.field: Default Invoice Owner mapped to a vendor

targetRef.field: automatic Invoice Owner assignment on extraction

configDependencies.condition: when an employee is mapped to a vendor, that employee is automatically assigned the invoice created on extraction whenever Capture Processing detects that vendor
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When you map an employee to a vendor, that employee is automatically assigned the invoice created on extraction in Capture Processing. This is done systematically by Concur Invoice when it detects that an owner exists for the vendor found in the invoice.

sourceRef.field: System Received Date visibility (Preferences Column Label list / Query Builder)

targetRef.field: System Received Date field on the Payment Request Header form

configDependencies.condition: the Capture Processing received-timestamp is only visible if the admin has first added the System Received Date field to the Payment Request Header form
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You can see the exact time when Concur Invoice received an invoice provided the admin has added the System Received Date field to the Payment Request Header form.

targetRef.field: quick search and advanced search field availability

configDependencies.condition: a field becomes usable in quick search and advanced search only when its Searchable flag is Yes; all added fields appear as vendor row grid columns regardless
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Note that while all fields can be added as columns in the vendor row grid, only selected fields can be used for the quick search and advanced search functionalities. This is represented as a _Yes_ or _No_ variable under the Searchable column on the Vendor Form page.

targetRef.field: fields visible in the end-user Search list, Advanced search window and vendor row grid

configDependencies.condition: users see only the set of fields the administrator adds with the Vendor Search Admin tool; qualified (searchable) fields appear in the Search list
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The user will see only the set of fields the administrator adds using the Vendor Search Admin tool (_Tax Type_ shown below). Qualified (searchable) fields appear in the Search list.

sourceRef.field: Limit processors, approvers or managers to use invoice owners vendor list

configDependencies.condition: the Invoice Settings restriction requires the Vendor Employee Access feature to be enabled for the company
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Use the Limit processors, approvers or managers to use invoice owners vendor list setting to restrict vendor selection to the vendors authorized for each employee. This setting requires the Vendor Employee Access feature to be enabled.

sourceRef.field: Limit processors, approvers or managers to use invoice owners vendor list

targetRef.field: vendor list available when changing a vendor

configDependencies.condition: when enabled, a processor changing a vendor sees the vendor list filtered to the same set available to the invoice's employee owner
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When a processor changes a vendor, this feature filters the vendor list to the same set available to the employee.

sourceRef.field: Vendor Form Name field added to the Payment Vendor form

targetRef.field: Vendor Manager visibility of vendors across different policy groups / vendor forms

configDependencies.condition: the Vendor Form Name field must first be added to the Payment Vendor form using the Forms and Fields tool; configuring it is what enables Vendor Managers to see and work with vendors belonging to different policy groups
configDependencies.sourceQuote: To enable the Vendor Form Name option, use the Forms and Fields tool to add the field to the Payment Vendor form.

sourceRef.field: Imaging Settings (unique company ID and public key)

configDependencies.condition: the unique company ID and public key must be supplied in the Imaging Settings section of Administration before an Invoice or Vendor Imaging Configuration is created in Image Handling
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Provide the unique company ID and public key by using the Imaging Settings section in Administration of Concur Invoice.

sourceRef.field: Imaging service included in the subscription

configDependencies.condition: step 1 of the imaging configuration chain: verify with the Concur Invoice administrator that the Imaging service is part of the standard subscription before configuring imaging
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Contact your Concur Invoice administrator to verify that the Imaging service is included in your standard subscription service.

configDependencies.condition: an imaging configuration must exist in Image Handling before it can be selected as the policy's Imaging Configuration
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You create imaging configurations in the Image Handling area of the Expense Configuration Administrator.

targetRef.field: imaging functionality active for the policy

configDependencies.condition: there is no default; imaging functionality is inactive for the policy unless an imaging configuration is selected
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select an imaging configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the imaging functionality will not be active for the policy.

configDependencies.condition: a scan configuration must be created on the Scan Configurations page in Image Handling before it can be assigned to a policy
configDependencies.sourceQuote: You create scan configurations on the Scan Configurations page in Image Handling.

targetRef.field: scan functionality active for the policy

configDependencies.condition: there is no default; scan functionality is inactive for the policy unless a scan configuration is selected
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select a scan configuration to be associated with this policy. There is no default value assigned; if you do not select a configuration, the scan functionality will not be active for the policy.

targetRef.field: scan configuration assignment scope (per policy, not per group; one per policy)

configDependencies.condition: scan configurations are assigned to policies rather than groups, so any group assigned to that policy inherits it; multiple scan configurations may exist but only one can be used per policy
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Scan configuration settings are not based on groups; they are assigned to specific policies enabling alerts and conditions to be configured for each policy. Therefore, any group assigned to a policy can use a scan configuration. An administrator can set up multiple scan configurations; however, only one scan configuration can be used per policy.

targetRef.field: Invoice Image Processor role capability (update Image Received information)

configDependencies.condition: once the Configuration admin has added a scan configuration, an employee assigned the Invoice Image Processor role can update the Image Received information for invoices in the groups the configuration applies to
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When the Configuration admin has added a scan configuration, an employee assigned the Invoice Image Processor role updates the Image Received information associated with an invoice.

sourceRef.field: Third-party digital tax invoice validator contract and SAP Concur feature enablement

targetRef.field: workflow and audit rules for digital tax invoice validation

configDependencies.condition: the client must contract with the validator and work with SAP Concur support to enable the feature before any workflow or audit rules for it can be configured
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The client must contract with the validator, and work with SAP Concur support to enable the feature and configure any desired workflow or audit rules.

configDependencies.condition: with a third-party validation service in use, any invoice with an attached XML file not validated as valid raises exception code INVXMLST, against which workflow rules can require processor review
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When a third-party validation service is in use, the processor will see an exception for any invoice with an attached XML file that has not been validated and determined to be valid. This exception uses the exception code INVXMLST, so workflow rules can be written to ensure that any invoice with this exception requires processor review.

sourceRef.field: e-Bunsho Timestamp feature enablement for Japan

configDependencies.condition: only when the e-Bunsho Timestamp feature for Japan is enabled can an Invoice Admin configure policy groups that require members to timestamp invoice images
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When the e-Bunsho Timestamp feature for Japan is enabled, an Invoice Admin can configure policy groups that require group members to timestamp invoice images before the related invoice is submitted for approval.

targetRef.field: Is Active for Group / Is Default Policy

configDependencies.condition: the e-Bunsho Timestamp Configuration is selected on the policy first, and only then is that policy activated (and optionally made default) for a group on Group Configurations
configDependencies.sourceQuote: To enable the e-Bunsho Timestamp feature for a policy and to activate the policy for a group:

sourceRef.field: e-Bunsho timestamp requirement on the policy group

configDependencies.condition: an invoice in an e-Bunsho policy group cannot be submitted for approval until its image has been successfully timestamped
configDependencies.sourceQuote: the invoice cannot be submitted for approval until the Invoice image has been successfully timestamped

sourceRef.field: Upload Image link in the Actions menu

configDependencies.condition: the Upload Image link appears to the employee only when the Allow employee to upload image files check box is selected on the imaging configuration
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select this check box if you want the Upload Image link to appear to the user in the Actions menu. Doing this allows the employee to click the link and upload images using the Upload Image window.

sourceRef.field: line item unit of measure on an imported/created supplier invoice

configDependencies.condition: error code 7001 (Invalid Unit of measure) is raised when the line item's unit of measure has not been added to the database, i.e. does not exist as a configured unit on the Units Of Measure page
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Line item unit of measure not added in database.

targetRef.field: default Unit of Measure value on a new item

configDependencies.condition: checking the box in the Default Goods or Default Services column makes that unit the default choice offered when a user of the matching spend type creates an item
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The administrator can specify a unit type that will always appear as the default choice by checking the box in the Default Goods or Default Services column.

targetRef.field: Unit of Measure field on Item forms (Purchase Request, PO, Payment Request)

configDependencies.condition: units are defined on the Units Of Measure page and the Unit of Measure field may then be added to any of the Item forms, where it offers those units
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Unit of Measure field may be added to any of the Item forms (Purchase Request, PO, and Payment Request)

configDependencies.condition: the Unit of Measure field may be included in PO matching rules and audit rules, so the units configured here are what those rules evaluate (it appears in the Detail-level field list on the Audit Rules Condition page)
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The field may be included in PO matching rules and audit rules

targetRef.field: Unit of Measure code in the import file

configDependencies.condition: units must exist on the Units Of Measure page before they can be supplied as values in a PO or Payment Request import
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The field may be included in a PO or Payment Request import

configDependencies.condition: The contents of the column B Data Object list are determined by the Event selected on the Audit Rule step; the event-to-object mapping itself is not enumerated in the corpus, only the dependency.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule. The administrator can create a condition based on:

configDependencies.condition: Column C Field/Value is populated from a helper pane whose contents are determined by the Data Object chosen in column B. Table 2 of the same topic is the per-data-object catalog of the Field/Value choices (Attendee Totals, Budget, Detail, Detail Allocation, Employee, Line Item Attendee, Purchase Request, Purchase Request Distribution, Purchase Request Item, Request, Request Exception, Vendor Remittance Address, Vendor Ship From Address).
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The information that appears in this pane is based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list.

configDependencies.condition: The field chosen in column C defines the data type of the condition, and the operator list offered in column D changes with that data type.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The list of operators changes depending on the type of data that is compared.

configDependencies.condition: When the selected field can hold multiple values, the operator carries an additional Any/Every qualifier that must be chosen; the qualifier only exists as a refinement of the operator.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: An operator is further defined by Any and Every depending on the type of data being compared.

configDependencies.condition: Choosing the Within operator changes the right-hand side into a date range expression evaluated against the two ends of the range, so the value entry semantics depend on the operator selected in column D.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Within operator defines a set of dates for the system to check against when evaluating the rule.

configDependencies.condition: Column E is pre-set by the system from the columns already completed (B, C, D) and is only overridden if needed.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The system provides the option that best suits the previous choices. Change it if necessary.

configDependencies.condition: Column F Field/Value is populated from a helper pane whose contents are determined by the Data Object chosen in column E, using the same per-object catalog as column C.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The information that appears in this pane is based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list.

configDependencies.condition: When the right-hand side of the condition is a second field rather than a constant, its data type must match the data type of the field chosen in column C.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If a second field is used in the condition, its data type must match that of the first field.

configDependencies.condition: The In and Not In operators turn the column F value control into a multi-select of expense types; the control's cardinality depends on the operator chosen in column D.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If you use the In or Not In operators for expense types, you can select multiple check boxes to include as many expense types as are required.

configDependencies.condition: Parenthesis balance constraint: the total count of right parentheses across the expression must equal the total count of left parentheses, with a maximum of three per side, so column G cannot be authored independently of column A.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: If a conditional expression contains parentheses, the count of left parentheses must match the count of right parentheses. There can be up to three parentheses for both left and right sides.

configDependencies.condition: Precedence constraint: there is no operator precedence between and and or, so the meaning of the And/Or joins is fixed entirely by parenthesis placement, or by strict left-to-right order when parentheses are omitted. Parentheses must therefore be authored with the joins in mind.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Parentheses are optional and used to define the order of operation for the and/or operators. If the parentheses are omitted, the and/or operations are carried out left to right. There is no precedence of and over or—the evaluation of the expression is simply left to right.

configDependencies.condition: The column H And/Or join only becomes meaningful once a further condition row exists to be joined to, so inserting an additional condition is what brings the join into play.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select either option to join the current condition to the next condition.

configDependencies.condition: A blank condition row must be inserted before its A-H columns can be filled in; where the row lands depends on which existing condition is selected first.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select Insert. The new blank row appears.

configDependencies.condition: Insert placement is positional: with no row selected the new condition is appended at the bottom, otherwise it is inserted above the currently selected condition, so authoring order of the condition list is controlled through Insert and Remove.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: To insert the new condition between existing conditions, select the condition that will be below the new condition.

configDependencies.condition: The Audit Rule step (Name, Event, Editable By, Applies To, Active) must be completed and Next selected before the Conditions step and its condition editor are reachable.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select Next. The Conditions step appears.

configDependencies.condition: All conditions must be authored on the Conditions step before Next opens the Exception step where visibility and the exception itself are set.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When all conditions have been added, select Next. The Exception step appears.

configDependencies.condition: In the new UI, Create on the Custom Rules page opens the Audit Rule step where Name and the other rule-level fields are entered.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: On the Custom Rules page, select Create. The Audit Rule step appears.

configDependencies.condition: In the legacy UI, New on the Custom page opens the Audit Rule step where Name and the other rule-level fields are entered.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: On the Custom page, select New. The Audit Rule step appears.

configDependencies.condition: Selecting an existing exception on the Exception step populates the audit rule's Exception Code, Exception Level, and Exception Text from the exception defined in Exceptions.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Use an existing exception. To use an existing exception, select the desired exception. It appears in the Exception Code, Exception Level, and Exception Text fields at the top of the page.

configDependencies.condition: A custom audit rule fired at Payment Request Submit raises its exception, and if that exception is above the exception level limit the invoice is blocked from submission and never enters the first workflow step.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Payment Request Submit: The rule is triggered when the invoice is submitted. If there are exceptions generated that are above the exception level limit (that is, prevents invoice submission; described in Exceptions in this guide), then the invoice will not be submitted and will not enter the first step of a workflow.

configDependencies.condition: Choosing Payment Post Request Submit places the rule after the invoice has already entered workflow, so exceptions it raises cannot block submission; the event choice determines whether the exception is a gate or an advisory flag.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Payment Post Request Submit: The rule is triggered immediately after an invoice enters the first step of workflow. Any exceptions generated will not prevent the invoice from being submitted.

configDependencies.condition: A random audit rule set to Payment Post Request Submit fires only after all approval and processor workflow steps have completed, so its position in the workflow is determined by the event selected on the Random tab.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Payment Post Request Submit: The rule is triggered when the invoice has gone through all the approval and processor workflow steps but before the pre-payment validation occurs.

configDependencies.condition: The exception level assigned to an audit rule's exception is what determines whether the rule blocks submission; the severity threshold at which blocking occurs is a client-defined setting.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The client can also define the point at which the severity of the exception prevents the user from submitting an invoice.

configDependencies.condition: The blocking threshold that gives an audit rule's exception level its effect is configured outside the Audit Rules page, in Invoice Admin Workflows.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The limit is set using the Invoice Admin, Workflows, and Settings.

configDependencies.condition: The same quote names Settings alongside Workflows as the location where the exception level blocking limit is set, so the audit rule's exception level is interpreted against an Invoice Settings value.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The limit is set using the Invoice Admin, Workflows, and Settings.

configDependencies.condition: A validation rule whose action is Exception only flags the line item or allocation, and whether that flag blocks invoice submission depends on the configured exception level settings.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Exception only: If the rule is triggered, it will flag the line item or line item allocation. Depending on your exception level settings, it may prevent invoice submission.

configDependencies.condition: Applies To is selected from a helper pane of group configurations, so the rule's scope is bound to configurations defined on the Group Configurations page.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select the field; the associated helper pane appears. Select the appropriate group(s).

configDependencies.condition: The Inherited/Not Inherited toggle only has meaning relative to the groups chosen in Applies To: it decides whether the rule also reaches the groups below those in the hierarchy.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Toggle Inherited/Not Inherited to indicate whether this rule will apply to the group(s) below this one in the hierarchical structure.

configDependencies.condition: The random rule's Applies To field is populated from the group configurations defined on the Group Configurations page.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In the Applies To field, select the appropriate group configuration(s) to which this rule applies.

configDependencies.condition: Editable By on the Random tab grants edit rights to named group configurations, which must exist on the Group Configurations page.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: In the Editable By field, select the group configuration(s) that can edit this rule.

configDependencies.condition: Activation of a random audit rule is constrained by its Applies To groups: only one random rule should be active per group configuration, otherwise selection results are unreliable.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Your company should have only one active random audit rule for each group configuration.

configDependencies.condition: The numeric count field in the Rule Type window is only entered when the Rule Type is Sequential.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Sequential and then enter the appropriate number

configDependencies.condition: The percentage field in the Rule Type window is only entered when the Rule Type is Percentage.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Percentage and then enter the appropriate percentage

configDependencies.condition: Selecting the Exception Code field on the Random tab opens the Exceptions window, from which an existing exception is used or a new one created.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Select the Exception Code field. The Exceptions window appears.

configDependencies.condition: Remove acts on the random rule currently selected in the Random tab grid, so a rule must be selected first.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: On the Random tab, select the rule you want to remove.

configDependencies.condition: On the Validation condition page, the column B Data Object list contents are determined by the event selected for the validation rule.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule:

configDependencies.condition: Column C's helper pane is driven by column B; when B is Field Validation, C lists the columns of the validation table instead of a data object's fields.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Field Validation: This will display the list of columns from the validation table.

configDependencies.condition: When the right-hand side is a Field Validation column, only validation-table columns whose data type matches the column selected in field C are offered in field F.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: Field Validation: This will display the list of columns from the validation table. Only columns that match the data type selected in field C above will display.

configDependencies.condition: List Validation is only offered in the second (column E) Data Object list, never in column B, so it can only ever form the right-hand side of a validation condition.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists and is only available on the second data object selection list.

configDependencies.condition: Selecting the List Validation object opens the List Validation Helper pane on the right of the condition page, listing the configured simple lists.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When the List Validation object is selected, the List Validation Helper pane will appear on the right side of the page, displaying the configured simple lists.

configDependencies.condition: Validation-table columns are unavailable as comparison operands unless the Field Validation data object is chosen in the Data Object list.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Field Validation data object must be selected in order to use fields in the validation table for comparison.

configDependencies.condition: Whenever the Field Validation data object is used, the Type column must be included among the conditions.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Type and Id 01 fields must be included when using the Field Validation data object.

configDependencies.condition: Whenever the Field Validation data object is used, the Id 01 column must be included among the conditions.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Type and Id 01 fields must be included when using the Field Validation data object.

configDependencies.condition: Id columns must be consumed contiguously in numeric order starting at Id 1, so using a higher Id requires every lower Id condition to exist first.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: When using the Field Validation object the Id fields must all be used in numeric order 1 through n. For example, if you use Id 5 you must use Id 1 through Id 4 first.

configDependencies.condition: The operator column is restricted to equal whenever the operand is an Id column, the Type column, or the Detail Allocation object.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator. This is the same for the Detail Allocation object.

configDependencies.condition: In validation conditions the Detail Allocation data object is confined to the right-hand side of the expression, so it can only be chosen in the second Data Object list.
configDependencies.sourceQuote: The Detail Allocation data object can only be on the right-hand side of the expression.

configDependencies.condition: Conditions using Entry State/Province must be authored with the Field Validation operand on the left and the State/Province field on the right, and the country sub codes must already be imported into the validation table.

configSteps.name: Create a new invoice policy and make it selectable by a group
configSteps.goal: A new, correctly-formed invoice policy exists with its forms, workflow, image handling and expense types set, and members of at least one group can actually pick it when they create an invoice (it is Active for the group, with a default settled).

sequence.action: select the row of an existing policy to use as the base
sequence.rationale: There is no blank-form creation path in 2026_08: creation IS copying, so a base row must be selected before the Copy Policy button has anything to act on. SOURCE: "You can create a new policy by copying an existing one and changing the information as it applies to the new policy." — concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/create-a-new-policy-dd9549c0.md

sequence.action: click
