sequence.rationale: 'Click Import.' → 'The system processes the data and the Import Summary window appears with the results of the import, including: Records Processed... Records Rejected...' then 'Review the information and then click Close. You will have the chance to review in detail the results displayed in this window in the next step.' (tools-guides/step-3-upload-and-import-template-and-data-b9a80bb6.md). The summary gives counts only — it tells you something was rejected but not what — so closing it is expected, not a skip. Note the tenant may also be configured for an overnight import job (tools-guides/over-night-hierarchy-mapping-import-available-059c9571.md), in which case rows may not be visible immediately.

sequence.action: Open View Import Details from the Actions menu and set the Type filter to Error
sequence.rationale: 'From the Actions menu, click View Import Details.' then filter with 'the Type list' where 'Error: Filters to display only the errors generated during import' (tools-guides/step-4-review-import-details-414c8cd5.md). This is documented as the step after the import for a reason — it is the only place the per-row cause is exposed. Reading Error before Warning before Info is a triage choice, not a corpus-stated order; the corpus only enumerates All / Error / Warning / Info as filter options.

sequence.action: Return to the Hierarchy Mapping List and search the imported mappings
sequence.rationale: 'On the Hierarchy Mapping List page, input the search criteria into the Search Routing Mappings search box' then 'Click the magnifying glass () icon to begin the search.' (tools-guides/search-for-hierarchy-mappings-1dea6bb6.md). Verification belongs after the error review, not instead of it: a partially rejected import still shows rows here, so searching first would give false confidence.

sequence.action: Verify a known mapping by Employee Last Name
sequence.rationale: 'Type the last name of the employee who is associated with the hierarchy mapping that you want to display. For example, if Ken Brown is associated with the mapping, type "Brown" in the Begins With search field.' (tools-guides/search-for-hierarchy-mappings-1dea6bb6.md). This is the owner-side check — it confirms the Employee ID column from order 3 resolved to a real employee rather than importing as an orphan string.

sequence.action: Verify the same mapping from the path side by segment
sequence.rationale: 'You can elect to search for the mapping by typing in any of the first three segments mappings. For example, if the mapping is Company > Sales > North, and you only remember North, select the correct sequence (Segment 3 in this example) and input North in the Begins With search field.' (tools-guides/search-for-hierarchy-mappings-1dea6bb6.md). Searching the path independently of the owner is what catches short-code errors from order 4 that still imported cleanly — the row exists, but under a path the AP user will never select. Note the corpus documents fallback behaviour rather than an error when the owner later leaves: 'If the specified user is not found (is promoted; transfers), the system will "walk" up the hierarchy to the very next logical employee and assign it to them.' (tools-guides/auto-assign-an-invoice-using-hierarchies-c4035783.md), which is why a Global Group default is advised: 'By designating a default, Global Group employee under the hierarchy, that employee will always be available to assign the invoice to.' (tools-guides/use-hierarchy-mappings-in-invoice-4fc3dff2.md).

configSteps.name: Build the Capture Processing forms and bind them to the Verification task
configSteps.goal: Stand up the Header, Line Item, and Vendor forms that OCR populates, then point the Verification task definition at them so a client-managed capture batch lands in a usable verification queue.

sequence.action: navigate and confirm landing tab
sequence.rationale: Path is 'Administration > Invoice > Capture Processing Admin' and the corpus states 'The page opens to the Capture Processing view of the Forms and Fields tab.' Starting here is not a preference — the whole tool is gated on a stated prerequisite: 'It is critical that these settings be configured prior to use. For example, the Client Managed Verification option for the Task Processor field must be selected, or the admin will not see either the Verification or Document Separation options.' If that activation is missing, later entries in this sequence have no controls to act on and the writer should abort rather than improvise. Note the tab is written 'Task Definition' here and 'Task Definitions' elsewhere in the same 2026_08 corpus — treat both spellings as the same tab.

sequence.action: copy a default Header form and add/rename fields on the Forms and Fields tab
sequence.rationale: Forms must exist before the Verification task can select them: 'The client will copy one or more default forms and rename them, after which each copied form is available for selection in the Task Definitions tab.' This is an explicit corpus ordering statement, not inference. Constrain additions against the enumerated auto-capture catalog (Vendor Name, Invoice Date, Invoice Number, Currency, Total Amount, Shipping, Tax, PO Number, Invoice Owner is configured, Vat 1, Vat Amount 1-4) because 'Fields may be added to the form but will require manual entry and coding by the Client-Managed Capture Verifier role' — a field added outside the catalog silently becomes manual labor, not automation.

sequence.action: copy a default Line Item form and place VAT fields deliberately
sequence.rationale: Same Forms-and-Fields-before-Task-Definitions dependency as order 2. Do the Line Item form in the same pass as the Header form because VAT placement across the two forms changes arithmetic, not just layout: 'If both the header and line item VAT fields have non-zero values, then the line item VAT placement has precedence and that will be considered for calculation, (header VAT values will be ignored in that case).' Deciding placement after the Header form is already bound risks a silent totals change on invoices already in flight.

sequence.action: configure the Vendor form and stop at Vendor Code
sequence.rationale: Third of the three forms the Verification task binds, so it belongs before order 5. Hard stop documented: 'The Capture Processing vendor form features a single field, Vendor Code, which is the only field that will be identified and captured when processing. Adding fields will not result in data in these fields being captured by the system.' Adding vendor fields here produces empty fields, not extra capture.

sequence.action: open the Task Definitions tab, select Verification, click Edit
sequence.rationale: Corpus procedure: '1. In Capture Processing, click the Task Definitions tab. 2. Select the definition and click Edit. 3. In the Modify Task Definition window, select options as detailed in the table below.' This is the only documented route to the form selectors and the disable flag, so it must precede orders 6-10.

sequence.action: confirm or set the task name in the Modify Task Definition window
sequence.rationale: Present on every task-definition row ('Task Def Name: The name of the task.'), so the writer should assert which definition is open before touching any repeated control. Necessary here because Disable Task Definition appears identically on four different definitions with different defaults — the task name is the only in-window evidence of which one is being edited.

sequence.action: select the Header form
sequence.rationale: Corpus: 'Forms (appear in Verification tab) — Header: Specify the header form to use' with the bound NOTE 'Fields for these forms are configured using options in the Forms and Fields tab.' The dropdown can only offer the copied form created at order 2, which is why the form build precedes selection.

sequence.action: select the Line Item form
sequence.rationale: 'Line Item: Specify the line item form to use' — same Forms-and-Fields dependency as order 7, consuming the form built at order 3. Selecting before the copy exists leaves the default form in place and the VAT placement decision unapplied.

sequence.action: select the Vendor form
sequence.rationale: 'Vendor: Specify the vendor form to use' — consumes the Vendor form from order 4. Grouping all three selectors before the disable flag is inference on my part; the corpus lists the three forms and the disable flag inside one table cell without ordering them.

sequence.action: verify Disable Task Definition remains No for Verification
sequence.rationale: 'Disable Task Definition: No (enabled) by default; select Yes (disabled) to disable verification.' Verified last in the window because it is the switch that makes everything above reachable — confirming it after the forms are bound means the writer never leaves a half-built form set attached to a disabled task. This is a read-and-confirm, not a change, unless the site is deliberately turning verification off.

sequence.action: enter Instruction Text for the Verifier
sequence.rationale: Location is version-sensitive and the writer must not look for it on Other Settings: revision history states 'The Instruction Text and Capture Attention To task settings are moved to the Task Definitions tab, under the Verification task definition.' It sits after the forms because its stated purpose is guidance for handling what the forms cannot capture — 'The Client Managed Capture Verifier role may need guidance when handling credit memos or other attachments.'

sequence.action: set Capture Attention To (Yes/No)
sequence.rationale: Last in this step because the correct value depends on a decision made on another page already in the graph: 'If the client is using the auto-routing features available using the Routing Configuration tool, the Capture Attention To option is not required and in fact should be disabled (No). The Routing Configuration takes precedence.' Setting Yes adds surface area to the Verification tab — 'The Capture Attention To option adds the optional Assign Invoice To field to the Invoice Details section of the Verification tab' — so check Routing Configuration state first, then set this.

configSteps.name: Stand up an email capture channel for a supplier intake stream
configSteps.goal: Create the alias that carries policy, language, and ownership attributes, hang a concursolutions.com capture address off it, set the fallback policies and exception recipient, then take control of how Concur answers that supplier's mail.

sequence.action: open Actions > Manage Email Alias > Add Alias from the Email Administration tab
sequence.rationale: Verbatim procedure: '1. Click Administration > Invoice > Capture Processing Admin > Email Administration tab. 2. Click Actions > Manage Email Alias > Add Alias.' The alias is built first because the alias is the attribute carrier — 'An email alias can be used to apply attributes to a group of email addresses associated with the alias' — and an address created before its alias exists has nothing to inherit from.

sequence.action: type the alias name
sequence.rationale: Step 3 of the same procedure: 'Type the name in Alias Name, and set the following optional attributes.' The name must be committed before the three optional attributes below, since they are described as attributes of this alias record.

sequence.action: select Policy Name for the alias
sequence.rationale: 'Policy Name: Select the policy that will be associated to invoices included in any batch emailed using this alias.' Depends on the Policies page (already in the graph) — the policy must exist there before it can be picked here. Watch the documented side effect: 'if a PO policy is invoked, the PO Number field is a Required field type as this number is essential to processing a purchase order' — choosing a PO policy type retroactively makes a Header field mandatory, so it interacts with the form built in step 1.

sequence.action: select Additional OCR Language
sequence.rationale: Enumerated as None / Japanese / Chinese with character-set precedence per option. Set here rather than later because of a stated override: 'The None setting is superseded if a language is configured in Modify Task Definition > Default Language.' If Default Language is configured in step 3 of this graph, leaving this at None does not mean Latin-only — the writer must not treat these two controls as independent.

sequence.action: set Owner Assignment to Sender if the sender should own the invoice
sequence.rationale: 'Owner Assignment: Select Sender to have the system automatically assign the invoice to the user sending the invoices via their From email address.' Corpus closes the alias procedure with 'Click Save, then click Close' — so all alias attributes are committed in one save, which is why orders 2-5 sit together before the address is created. Only Sender is documented as a value; do not invent others.

sequence.action: add the capture email address in the Add Email window
sequence.rationale: Comes after the alias so the address can be associated to it: 'The Email Administration tab includes options that let the admin add email addresses and associate these email addresses to an email alias.' Format is not free-form — 'The email requires the following format, with no spaces: CompanyName + InvoiceCapture + @concursolutions.com - OR - Domain + InvoiceCapture + @concursolutions.com'. Also note the activation trap that blocks later steps: 'WARNING At this time, send a minimum of one batch to the email address configured for the client to expose the email address in the Email Administration tab of the Capture Processing Admin tool.'

sequence.action: select the capture type for the address
sequence.rationale: Dual-support control on the same Add Email page, set in the same pass as the address: 'With both capture types available, the admin can add an email, then specify the capture type they want matched to the address' — the word 'then' is the corpus's own ordering. Consequence if skipped: 'batches are pre-set to the capture type based entirely on the email address the batch was sent to', so an unset capture type mis-sorts every batch on that channel.

sequence.action: set Default Policy for Email on the Other Settings tab
sequence.rationale: Placed after the alias policy because it is the fallback, not the primary: the alias policy applies to batches emailed using that alias, while this sets the tab-level default that 'will populate the Policy field for emailed and uploaded batches in the Verification page.' Ordering the specific (alias) before the general (tab default) is my inference — the corpus documents both but never states which to configure first.

sequence.action: set Default Policy for Upload on the Other Settings tab
sequence.rationale: Sibling control on the same tab, covering the other sending method: 'The default policy options let the administrator set a default policy under which each of the batches, based on the sending method (upload and email), will inherit their policy attributes.' Set alongside order 8 so email and upload channels cannot drift onto different policies by omission.

sequence.action: enter the Exception Email Address (semicolon-separated)
sequence.rationale: Corpus procedure step 1 on this tab: 'On the Other Settings tab, type an email address in Exception Email Address. To add multiple email addresses, separate the additional email addresses using a semi-colon.' Do this before the channel goes live, because unprocessable mail is silently discarded from the operator's view otherwise — 'When the system encounters an email that cannot be processed (unsupported document type; credit memos), the original email is formatted into a single PDF document that is sent as an attachment in the exception email notification to the recipient specified in Exception Email Address.' Corpus TIP: 'Create a dedicated email alias (email distribution list) that includes all AP department/Verifiers.'

sequence.action: set Enable Vendor Segregation to Yes
sequence.rationale: Strictly after orders 1-7, because segregation is built on the alias-to-address association created there: 'By associating email addresses to a single email alias, and then assigning the alias to a group of vendors, only those vendors are available during the OCR step, and when changing vendors manually during the verification step.' Turning it on before the alias and address exist yields a filter with nothing to filter by. Activation instruction: 'To activate this feature, select Yes from the Enable Vendor Segregation list.' Only Yes is enumerated in the corpus.

sequence.action: search the address on Supplier Email Administration and click Edit Email
sequence.rationale: Last position is forced by the warning at order 6 — the address is not exposed in the tool until at least one batch has been sent to it, so this control cannot be reached on a brand-new channel. Corpus route: 'The admin searches for the email by its address, and then clicks Edit Email to open the Edit Email window.'

sequence.action: set Block Incoming Emails
sequence.rationale: 'Block Incoming Emails: (Default = No) Capture Processing will prevent a supplier email from being received or displayed based on the email address associated with that supplier.' Only reachable via the Edit Email window opened at order 12. Leave at No for a channel being stood up; the documented uses are to 'temporarily disable selected emails, archive, and accept a different email address from a supplier changing location or domain, block spam.'

sequence.action: set Send Email Acknowledgement
sequence.rationale: Same Edit Email window, so it follows order 12. Corpus wording is internally awkward and the writer should record the default rather than reason about the prose: 'Send Email Acknowledgement: (Default = No) Capture Processing will send an acknowledgement to the supplier on receipt of their email unless the admin selects No to prevent this email from being generated and sent.' Decide it last because it is the only control here that emits outbound mail to the supplier — do not flip it before the intake channel is confirmed working.

configSteps.name: Switch to automated document separation and settle the verifier's coding defaults
configSteps.goal: Flip the paired separation task definitions together, set extraction language and default ledger so Capture Processing output codes correctly, then make vendors findable and units of measure coherent for the manual work that remains.

sequence.action: open the Task Definitions tab and edit the Document Separation definition
sequence.rationale: Same documented entry point as step 1 ('Select the definition and click Edit'). The corpus warns this is not a default-accepting area: 'In most situations, the administrator should accept the default settings as they support full use of the feature. However, if a site wishes to change the separation task from manual to automatic, selected definitions must be configured to do so.'

sequence.action: set Disable Task Definition to Yes on Document Separation
sequence.rationale: Half of a mandatory pair: 'Disable Task Definition: No (enabled) by default; select Yes (disabled) in conjunction with selecting No in the Automated Document Separation definition to have the system perform automated (not manual) separation of document pages to processing-ready state.' The corpus states the pairing ('in conjunction with') but never states which of the two to change first — putting manual-off before automated-on is my inference, chosen so the writer never leaves both separation methods enabled simultaneously. The corpus is explicit that these two are one control surface: 'the separation tasks work in tandem by requiring that both separation definitions be modified to change the functionality of the separation overall.'

sequence.action: set Disable Task Definition to No on Automated Document Separation
sequence.rationale: The other half, and it must not be left undone: 'Disable Task Definition: Yes (disabled) by default; select No (enabled) in conjunction with selecting Yes in the Document Separation definition.' Note the inverted default versus its sibling — same control name, opposite starting value, which is exactly the trap a writer walks into if it treats the two rows as identical. Operational precondition to surface before enabling: this task 'requires the use of separator pages between invoices', so enabling it without the physical separator pages breaks batches rather than automating them.

sequence.action: confirm Disable Task Definition remains No on Content Extraction
sequence.rationale: 'Disable Task Definition: No (enabled) by default; select Yes (disabled) to disable content extraction.' Checked before setting Default Language because Default Language is a field of the Content Extraction definition — configuring a language on a disabled extraction task is a no-op the UI will still accept.

sequence.action: set Default Language on the Content Extraction definition
sequence.rationale: 'Default Language: Set the default language used on extraction.' Deliberately sequenced after the alias work in the previous step because this control silently outranks it: 'The None setting is superseded if a language is configured in Modify Task Definition > Default Language.' A writer that sets this first and the alias language second will produce a configuration whose alias-level None is misleading.

sequence.action: select Default Ledger on the Other Settings tab
sequence.rationale: 'Clients using more than one ledger at their company can specify which ledger they want associated with the invoice output generated by Capture Processing.' Position it after separation and extraction are settled because it governs the output those tasks produce, and the failure mode is silent and accounting-visible: 'Doing this prevents incorrect account codes from being unintentionally associated with invoices created in Capture Processing.' Applies only where more than one ledger exists; skip otherwise rather than guessing a value.

sequence.action: add or remove vendor search fields via Administration > Invoice > Vendor Search Admin (left menu)
sequence.rationale: Placed after Enable Vendor Segregation (previous step) because segregation decides which vendors a verifier may pick and this page decides how they find them — the pairing is my inference; the corpus documents no dependency between the two pages. Purpose, verbatim: 'This page is used to add or remove the fields that will appear for the user when searching for vendors.' Be aware the entire admin reference for this page lives in the Tools Guides deliverable; no admin-guide topic covers it in 2026_08.

sequence.action: confirm the Searchable Yes/No value for each field added
sequence.rationale: Immediately after adding a field, because adding is not the same as making it searchable: 'Note that while all fields can be added as columns in the vendor row grid, only selected fields can be used for the quick search and advanced search functionalities. This is represented as a Yes or No variable under the Searchable column on the Vendor Form page.' A writer that stops at order 7 produces grid columns the verifier cannot search on. Note the attribute is documented as living on the Vendor Form page; the corpus does not state that page and Vendor Search Admin are the same grid, so treat it as a second location to visit.

sequence.action: add or edit units and set their spend type
sequence.rationale: Reached at Administration > Invoice > Units Of Measure. Units must exist before anything can reference them — the corpus lists three downstream consumers: 'The Unit of Measure field may be added to any of the Item forms (Purchase Request, PO, and Payment Request)', 'The field may be included in PO matching rules and audit rules', and 'The field may be included in a PO or Payment Request import'. Ordering this before Audit Rules (already in the graph) is inference: the corpus states the field may be used in audit rules but does not state a configuration sequence. Values are enumerated: 'Units are associated with a spend type (Goods, Services, or Both).' This page is also open to the Restricted role, unlike most of Group 4.

sequence.action: check Default Goods on the unit that should preselect for Goods items
sequence.rationale: After order 9, because a unit must exist and carry a spend type before it can be the default for that type: 'The administrator can specify a unit type that will always appear as the default choice by checking the box in the Default Goods or Default Services column.' Effect is at item-entry time — 'the default selection for Goods is the one specified as the default in Units of Measure above.'

sequence.action: check Default Services on the unit that should preselect for Services items
sequence.rationale: Parallel control for the other spend type, from the same sentence as order 10. Set both in one pass so Goods and Services do not end up with one defaulted and one not; the corpus notes 'Units of measure appear when a PR item is added and vary depending on the spend type', so a missing default on one type shows up only for that type's users.

configSteps.name: Configure image handling so uploaded and scanned invoices attach and are trackable
configSteps.goal: Create the imaging configuration a policy can consume, allow employee uploads, then add a scan configuration for barcode-tracked paper and bind it to the policy that governs those invoices.

sequence.action: navigate and pick Invoice Imaging or Vendor Imaging
sequence.rationale: Route: 'Click Administration > Invoice (on the sub-menu). Click Image Handling (left menu). The Image Handling window appears.' The tab choice is first and mutually exclusive — the corpus writes it as 'Either: Click the Invoice Imaging tab. – or – Click the Vendor Imaging tab.' The configuration row created next belongs to whichever tab is active, so picking after creating the row is not possible. For vendor-side setup the corpus also names a separate page entirely: '...or, for vendors, Administration > Invoice > Vendor Handling.'

sequence.action: click the default row to edit, or click New for a fresh configuration
sequence.rationale: Step 4 of the procedure, again an either/or: 'Click the default row to edit the existing default configuration. – or – Click New to create a new configuration. A new row appears.' Editing the default silently changes every policy already pointing at it, whereas New leaves existing policies untouched — the writer must decide this before typing a name, not after. Multiple configurations are expected: 'Since a configuration is assigned to a policy, several configurations can be created to be used depending on geographical region, etc.'

sequence.action: enter the configuration Name
sequence.rationale: First field in the row and the one the downstream page consumes: 'Enter a unique name for the configuration. This name will appear as an option when setting up policies.' Uniqueness is required here (unlike scan configuration names), and the name is the only handle the Policies page has on this record.

sequence.action: enter the Acrobat Reader Download URL
sequence.rationale: 'Enter the link to the Adobe Web site where the employee can download the software. The link appears in the error message that displays when the system checks to see if Adobe Reader is installed.' Set before enabling uploads (order 7) because it is the recovery path shown to the employee at the exact moment the check fails — an empty value turns a solvable error into a dead end.

sequence.action: set the Mark invoices received on successful image check checkbox
sequence.rationale: 'Select this check box if you want the system to note the invoices as received when they have transmitted successfully.' Decide it in the same row edit as the other fields, before Save. Bound caveat that should be reflected to the operator: 'NOTE: The employee must verify the clarity and accuracy of the successful transmission of invoices' — the automatic received marking is a transmission signal, not a quality signal.

sequence.action: confirm the accepted file types before opening upload to employees
sequence.rationale: A verification entry, not a settable control — checked before order 7 so the rollout message matches reality. The admin-guides list enumerates TIF, TIFF, JPEG, JPG, PNG, PDF (with XFA; with embedded fonts), Word file (DOC; DOCX), Excel file (XLS; XLSX – not supported: XLTS), EML (File saved using Microsoft Outlook), CSV. Flag the discrepancy rather than reconciling it: the tools-guides sibling topic adds 'CFDi (tax information with PDF)' and drops the XLTS caveat, and a third corpus list covering emails and uploads is narrower still (PNG, JPG, JPEG, PDF, TIF, TIFF, HTML with no double-byte characters).

sequence.action: select Allow employee to upload image files
sequence.rationale: 'Select this check box if you want the Upload Image link to appear to the user in the Actions menu. Doing this allows the employee to click the link and upload images using the Upload Image window.' This is the control that exposes the feature to end users, so it goes after the supporting fields at orders 4-6 are populated. Blocking condition the writer must report rather than work around: 'Note: If this option is not displayed, submit a service request to have this feature turned on.'

sequence.action: click Save on the imaging configuration
sequence.rationale: Procedure step 6, 'Click Save.' Mandatory before any policy work: the umbrella guide orders the whole feature as 'Create an Invoice Imaging Configuration in Administration > Invoice > Image Handling as the Invoice Configuration Administrator' then 'Assign an imaging configuration to a policy in Administration > Invoice > Policies.' An unsaved row does not appear in the Policies list.

sequence.action: record the Upload Image session limit as an operator note, do not attempt to set it
sequence.rationale: Explicitly a read-only runtime constraint on the end-user Upload Image window — a writer that treats it as a numeric admin input will fail looking for a field that does not exist. Bound facts: the limit is 10 files per session, it is repeatable ('To upload more than 10, simple upload the first 10 and then upload another 10, until done'), sessions accumulate ('Multiple sessions can be initiated for a single invoice or vendor request; files are appended to prior uploads for a given invoice'), and the per-file size cap is never stated numerically in the corpus — 'There is a size limit for each image file; the Upload Image window (shown below) displays that limit.' Companion guidance worth passing on: 'When scanning, the images should be scanned at 300 dpi or lower to reduce file size.'

sequence.action: click the Scan Configurations tab
sequence.rationale: Separate sub-feature on the same page, started only after the imaging configuration is saved so the two records are not half-built at once. Corpus route: 'Click Image Handling (left menu). The Image Handling page appears. Click the Scan Configurations tab.' Skip this entire block for sites that do not track paper — scan configuration exists for 'Companies that track paper invoices manually by using barcode technology.'

sequence.action: click New to add a scan configuration row
sequence.rationale: 'Click New. A new row appears ready for input.' The row must exist before its two fields can be typed, and before Policies can offer it at order 15.

sequence.action: enter the Configuration Name
sequence.rationale: 'This is the name of the scan configuration. The name does not need to be unique for each configuration; however, SAP Concur recommends that you use names that are easy to understand and to recognize in the list.' Note the contrast with order 3 — uniqueness is required for the imaging configuration name and explicitly not required here, so name collisions are possible and only the writer's discipline prevents an ambiguous Policies list.

sequence.action: set Image Invoice Container ID Required to Yes or No
sequence.rationale: 'Select Yes or No in the list.' Decide before Save because Yes imposes work on a different role on a different page: 'If Yes, the invoice image processor must populate the Image Invoice Container ID field for invoices associated with this scan configuration on the Process Images page.' Setting Yes without briefing that role stalls image processing.

sequence.action: click Save on the scan configuration
sequence.rationale: 'Click Save. The new configuration appears on the page.' The corpus then states the binding requirement outright: 'Once you have created a scan configuration, you must it assign it to a policy' — so Save is the hinge between this page and order 15, and an unsaved row cannot be assigned.

sequence.action: select the policy, click Modify, and pick the scan configuration
sequence.rationale: Explicit corpus ordering (Step 2 follows Step 1): 'Click Administration > Invoice. Click Policies (left menu)... Select the desired policy. Click Modify... Select the appropriate scan configuration name from the Scan Configuration list. This is the name that you created on the Scan Configuration page in Image Handling.' Cardinality constrains how many times this runs: 'One configuration can be used by multiple policies; however, each policy can only use a single scan configuration.' Assignment is per policy, not per group — 'Scan configuration settings are not based on groups; they are assigned to specific policies.'

sequence.action: select the Timestamp Configuration value if e-Bunsho timestamping is in scope
sequence.rationale: Optional and Japan-specific, and it is NOT an Image Handling control despite belonging to the imaging story — 'On the Administration >Invoice > Policies page, when Invoice Admins modify a policy, the admin will see the Timestamp Configuration field.' Grouped here with order 15 because both are policy-level bindings and the writer is already in Modify Policy. Only one value is named anywhere in the corpus (Japan e-Bunsho); do not assume others. Downstream work continues on Group Configurations (Policies column > Modify > Is Active for Group / Is Default Policy), and image eligibility is physical: 'To be eligible for an e-Bunsho timestamp, images must be more than 200dpi (scanner) or 3.88M pixels (smartphone/digital camera) and at least 24-bit color for RGB.'

sequence.action: open the Exceptions helper pane to add an image-related exception code
sequence.rationale: Last because exceptions describe failures of the pipeline built at orders 1-15 — defining them before the configurations exist means guessing at what can fail. The pane is reachable from inside the Image Handling tool (shared with Audit Rules, Workflows, and Invoice Processor), the alternative entry being 'From within the Exceptions tool'. Visibility gate the writer must check before reporting failure: 'Group administrators can only add exceptions if given create rights for the Invoice Configuration Administrator. If the administrator does not have permissions, the New link does not appear.' The exception attributes themselves are Exceptions-tool fields, not Image Handling fields, and are not configured from this sequence.

configSteps.name: Author a Custom audit rule with a multi-condition expression
configSteps.goal: Create a Custom-tab audit rule end to end, exercising all EIGHT condition-editor columns (A Left Parenthesis, B Data Object, C Field/Value, D Operator, E Data Object, F Field/Value, G Right Parenthesis, H And/Or), joining two or more conditions with And/Or and balanced parentheses, then attaching an exception.

sequence.action: select menu
sequence.rationale: Corpus-stated first step. access-custom-audit-70726665.md: 'Select Administration > Invoice.' Nothing in Audit Rules is addressable before this menu is opened. d8c64dd4 adds that 'Depending on your permissions, the page may appear immediately after you select Administration.'

sequence.action: select left-menu item
sequence.rationale: Corpus-stated second step: 'Select Audit Rules (left menu). The Audit Rules page appears.' The Custom / Random / Validation tab strip only exists once this page is rendered, so every downstream tab choice depends on it.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: NEW UI variant only. add-a-custom-audit-rule-0f1d320e.md: 'On the Custom Rules page, select Create. The Audit Rule step appears.' Entering the wizard must precede any field entry. Same control as CustomRuleCreateButton.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: LEGACY UI variant only — occupies the SAME position as order 3, not an additional action. add-a-custom-audit-rule-43e3f9aa.md: 'On the Custom page, select New. The Audit Rule step appears.' The two files are otherwise identical; only the page label (Custom Rules vs Custom) and the button label differ. Same control as CustomRuleNewButton. Perform one or the other, never both.

sequence.action: type
sequence.rationale: 'Type a unique name.' First row of the Audit Rule step's field table. Position within the step follows the table's row order — that ordering is INFERRED, since the corpus gives the fields as a description table, not a numbered sequence.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: 'Select the event that triggers the rule' — Allocation Save, Payment Request Details Save/Submit, Payment Request Save/Submit, Payment Post Request Submit. This position is CORPUS-STATED as a dependency, not table order: the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md says of column B, 'The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule.' Event therefore gates the entire Conditions step and must be committed before Next. Note the wider superset in custom_audit_rule_event (Purchase Order / Purchase Request events) is documented in audit-rules-257356ed.md as available 'in Administration > Invoice > Audit Rules when creating the audit rule' — it does not appear in the Add a Custom Audit Rule field table itself.

sequence.action: open helper pane and select groups
sequence.rationale: 'This field defaults to your access rights. Change it if necessary. Select the field; the associated helper pane appears. Select the appropriate group(s).' It is pre-populated, so it can be left alone; its position relative to Applies To is table order (INFERRED).

sequence.action: open helper pane and select groups
sequence.rationale: 'Select the field; the associated helper pane appears. Select the appropriate group(s).' Must precede the Inherited toggle because the toggle qualifies this selection.

sequence.action: toggle
sequence.rationale: 'Toggle Inherited/Not Inherited to indicate whether this rule will apply to the group(s) below this one in the hierarchical structure.' Corpus binds this toggle to Applies To, so it necessarily follows group selection — that dependency is stated, the adjacency is not.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: 'Select Yes to activate the rule upon completion.' Last row of the table. 'Upon completion' means the value is only honoured when the wizard finishes, so it may in practice be set any time before Done — placing it last is INFERRED from table order.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Next. The Conditions step appears.' Corpus-stated transition; the condition editor does not exist until this fires.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column A of the eight-column editor. the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md: 'A: Left Parenthesis — Select zero to three parentheses, depending on the complexity of the condition.' First because the corpus letters the columns A through H left to right; the letters are corpus-stated, the left-to-right fill order is INFERRED from them. understand-conditional-expressions-97cf41ea.md constrains the whole expression: 'the count of left parentheses must match the count of right parentheses. There can be up to three parentheses for both left and right sides.'

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column B — THE COLUMN THE PRIOR BUILD MISSED, and the one that gates everything downstream. 'B: Data Object — The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule.' Enumerated: Attendee Totals, Budget, Detail, Detail Allocation, Employee, Line Item Attendee, Request, Request Exception, Vendor Remittance, Vendor Ship From. It must be set before column C because C's helper pane content is derived from it.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Alias of order 13 — same column B under its letter-suffixed field id, same enumerated list. Not a second action.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Alias of order 13 — same column B under its unprefixed field id, as the parity pages name it (conditional-expressions-and-the-condition-page-4d98af34.md, the-query-builder-and-the-condition-editor-e10473f9.md, which label the column simply 'Data Object'). Not a second action.

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Column C. 'C: Field/Value — Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list. See Table 2.' Table 2 of the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md is the per-data-object field catalog (~250 names across 13 objects) — the artefact skipped entirely last time. It is a helper PANE, not an inline dropdown, so it opens only after B is chosen. Counts per object are captured in the value sets (Attendee Totals 4, Budget 15, Detail 21, Detail Allocation 5, Employee 26, Line Item Attendee 13, Purchase Request 24, Purchase Request Distribution 3, Purchase Request Item 21, Request 97, Request Exception 2, Vendor Remittance Address 29, Vendor Ship From Address 18). Note the catalog carries three Purchase Request objects and spells the vendor objects 'Vendor Remittance Address' / 'Vendor Ship From Address', which do not match column B's own list verbatim — record that mismatch, do not reconcile it.

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Alias of order 16 — same column C under its unprefixed field id. Not a second action.

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Column D. 'D: Operator — Select an item from the helper pane that appears. The information that appears in this pane is based upon your previous choices.' Third in the chain because the operator list is derived from the C field's data type: understand-conditional-expressions-97cf41ea.md, 'The list of operators changes depending on the type of data that is compared.' Corpus note: 'If you use the In or Not In operators for expense types, you can select multiple check boxes to include as many expense types as are required.'

sequence.action: choose Any or Every qualifier
sequence.rationale: Sub-choice on the operator, only surfaced when the selected field can hold multiple values. Position is immediately after D because it qualifies D. CORPUS-STATED for the Validation tab (the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md: 'When a field with multiple values is selected, the administrator must choose whether the condition will fire if Any or Every value matches') and for conditional expressions generally (understand-conditional-expressions-9a165c46.md defines ANY as 'Where a single expense of many associated with the report is true for the operator' and EVERY as 'Where all expenses associated with the report are true for the operator'). Its presence on the CUSTOM tab is INFERRED from those two, since the Custom-tab condition page does not restate it.

sequence.action: select Within operator and enter its date offset
sequence.rationale: A specific value of column D whose semantics change what column F means. the-condition-page-3408dec8.md: 'The Within operator defines a set of dates for the system to check against when evaluating the rule. For example, if you use Within Today -2 to evaluate the Request Submit Date, the system will look for the submit dates within the two ends of the range: Today, and two days earlier.' That page documents Print Condition Rules and states it 'is similar to the Condition page used for Audit Rules and Invoice Processor' — so applicability to the Custom Audit tab is INFERRED from the stated similarity, not asserted directly.

sequence.action: confirm or change auto-selected value
sequence.rationale: Column E. 'E: Data Object — The system provides the option that best suits the previous choices. Change it if necessary.' CORPUS-STATED to be auto-populated from the earlier choices, so it necessarily sits after D — this is the one ordering in the editor the corpus pins rather than implies. On the parity Query Builder page the equivalent right-hand object is fixed ('This field will always display as Value and you cannot change this'), which the Audit Rules page explicitly does not say; do not carry that constraint over.

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Column F, the right-hand operand. Same helper-pane mechanic and same Table 2 catalog as column C. Data-type constraint from understand-conditional-expressions-97cf41ea.md: 'If you use a second field in the condition, you must ensure its data type matches that of the first field.'

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Alias of order 22 — same column F under its unprefixed field id. Not a second action.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column G. 'G: Right Parenthesis — Select zero to three parentheses, depending on the complexity of the condition.' Placed after F because it closes the operand it wraps. Balance rule is expression-wide, not row-wide: the corpus's own counter-examples 'Condition1 ) And ( Condition2' and '( Condition1 )) And ( Condition2' are called incorrect 'even though the total left/right count matches', so placement is validated across rows.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column H — the join to the NEXT condition, so it is meaningful only once a second row exists. 'H: And/Or — Select either option to join the current condition to the next condition.' The Workflow parity page adds that this line 'appears when there are multiple conditions, and only between conditions, never after the final condition', and the Query Builder page: 'Appears only where two or more conditions are referenced.' The unprefixed alias and_or carries the lowercase 'and'/'or' rendering used in the prose ('each condition is separated by either and or or'); condition_and_or carries the title-case UI labels. There is no operator precedence — 'There is no precedence of and over or, the evaluation of the expression is simply left to right.'

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: Adds the second (and each later) condition row, so it comes AFTER the first row is complete. 'Complete all conditions using these same steps, using Insert to add conditions and Remove to delete conditions. If you simply select Insert, a new condition appears at the bottom. To insert the new condition between existing conditions, select the condition that will be below the new condition.' That last sentence makes row selection a prerequisite for mid-list insertion — a corpus-stated ordering. 'There is no limit to the number of conditions that comprise a total expression.' Then repeat orders 12-25 for each new row.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: Deletes a condition row. Same list-editing pass as Insert, hence adjacent to it; the corpus names them in one breath ('using Insert to add conditions and Remove to delete conditions') and gives no separate procedure, so relative order is INFERRED.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'When all conditions have been added, select Next. The Exception step appears.' Corpus-stated gate: the whole expression is completed before the exception is defined.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: 'From the Exception Visibility list, select the users who are able to see the exception message.' First on the Exception step and stated before the existing-vs-new branch, because visibility is applied to the use of the exception rather than to the exception record: exception-helper-within-the-audit-rules-and-workflow-tools-07dfd781.md — 'This is not attached to the exception itself, but can be generated individually each time the exception is used, such as within the Audit Rules tool.'

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: Branch point. Either select an existing exception — 'It appears in the Exception Code, Exception Level, and Exception Text fields at the top of the page' — or 'Select New. The New Exception window appears.' Orders 31-33 apply only to the New branch.

sequence.action: type
sequence.rationale: One of the three fields the corpus names for an exception (code, level, text). Inside the New Exception window, so it follows order 30. The corpus says only 'Complete the fields' — the internal order of 31-33 is INFERRED from the order they are listed in step 9 of add-a-custom-audit-rule and in summary-the-basic-process-of-creating-random-audit-rules-e794c09f.md.

sequence.action: set level
sequence.rationale: Second of the three exception attributes. Load-bearing beyond labelling: the level decides whether the rule merely flags or blocks — add-a-validation-rule-0b31c4c0.md, 'If there are exceptions generated that are above the exception level limit (that is, prevents invoice submission)... then the invoice will not be submitted and will not enter the first step of a workflow.'

sequence.action: type
sequence.rationale: Third exception attribute — the message the audience chosen in order 29 will see.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Save.' Closes the New Exception window and returns to the Exception step; must precede Done because Done consumes the selected exception.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Done.' Final corpus-stated action of the Custom rule wizard. The validation-rule wording makes the return state explicit — 'The exception you created is pre-selected. Select Done to include the exception with the...rule and finish this task.'

configSteps.name: Author a Validation rule (four-step wizard, distinct condition semantics)
configSteps.goal: Create a Validation-tab rule through its own four-step wizard — Validation Rule, Conditions, Actions, Exception — using the VALIDATION condition editor, whose Data Object lists and helper panes are different from the Custom tab's and must not be reused from it.

sequence.action: select menu
sequence.rationale: access-validation-rules-5f8dbf9e.md step 1: 'Select Administration   Invoice.' Same entry point as the Custom path.

sequence.action: select left-menu item
sequence.rationale: 'Select Audit Rules (left menu). The Audit Rules page appears.' Validation is a tab on the Audit Rules page, not a separate admin tool.

sequence.action: select tab
sequence.rationale: 'Select Validation.' Note the corpus is inconsistent about the control's noun: access-validation-rules-5f8dbf9e.md says only 'Select Validation', while the lifecycle pages say 'On the Validation tab' (edit-a-validation-rule-d8635d4a.md) and 'On the Validation page' (add/delete/deactivate). No distinct field id exists for the tab itself, so it is recorded here against the Audit Rules navigation. Do not invent one.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'On the Validation page, select New. The page refreshes into a four-step wizard, starting with the Validation Rule page.' Corpus-stated. Two differences from the Custom tab worth recording: the button is New in BOTH variants (there is no Create-labelled new-UI counterpart documented), and the wizard has FOUR steps, not three.

sequence.action: type
sequence.rationale: Labelled 'Validation Rule Name' on this page: 'Type the name of the rule.' First row of the field table; position INFERRED from table order.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Must precede the Conditions step for the same corpus-stated reason as the Custom tab — the-validation-condition-page-8b2a2704.md, column B: 'The choices that appear in this list are based on the event that triggers the rule.' The Validation event list is its own set (12 values, including Payment Request Distribution Save, Purchase Request Save/Submit and Purchase Request Item Save) and is NOT the Custom tab's six-value list; each carries a distinct trigger description, e.g. Payment Request Allocation Save 'is triggered when each invoice allocation is saved.' One entry, Payment Post Request Submit, is documented with an unresolved editorial placeholder — record it as enumerated but undescribed.

sequence.action: select True or False
sequence.rationale: POSITION AND FIELD BOTH FLAGGED. The corpus row here is 'Execute action when validation condition is:' with values True and False — a control that has NO counterpart on the Custom tab and NO field id in the supplied set. It sits between Event and Editable By Groups in the field table. Recorded against the nearest listed control only as a placeholder; the True/False selector needs its own field and must not be conflated with Active. Do not fabricate values for it beyond the two the corpus enumerates.

sequence.action: open helper pane and select groups
sequence.rationale: Labelled 'Editable By Groups' here (the Custom tab says 'Editable By'): 'Click the link; the associated helper pane appears. Select the appropriate group(s).' Note it is described as a LINK on this page and as a field on the Custom page. Position is table order — INFERRED.

sequence.action: open helper pane and select groups
sequence.rationale: Labelled 'Applies To Groups': 'Click the link; the associated helper pane appears.' The Validation field table does NOT document an Inherited/Not Inherited toggle, though summary-the-basic-process-of-creating-validation-rules-7f36bed3.md says the administrator 'Identifies the group to which the rule applies and whether the rule is inherited to the groups below it'. Inheritance is therefore attested in the summary but has no documented control on this page — do not import the Custom tab's inherited_toggle.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: 'Select Yes (if necessary) to activate the rule upon completion.' Last row of the table; position INFERRED. The '(if necessary)' hedge is absent from the Custom tab's identical row.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Next. The Conditions page appears.' First of three Next transitions in this wizard.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column A of the VALIDATION condition editor: 'A: Left Parenthesis — Select zero to three parentheses.' The unprefixed parenthesis/operator/and-or ids are used on this page because the corpus documents columns A, D, G and H identically across the Custom and Validation editors and supplies validation-specific ids only for B, C, E and F. Same balance rule applies.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column B — and THE key divergence from the Custom tab. Its list is eight values: Detail, Detail Allocation, Employee, Field Validation, Request, Request Exception, Vendor Remittance Address, Vendor Ship From Address. Attendee Totals, Budget and Line Item Attendee are absent; Field Validation is present and has no Custom-tab counterpart; the two vendor objects are spelled with 'Address'. Reusing the Custom tab's list here was the prior build's error. Gates column C, so it precedes it.

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Column C. Generic behaviour matches the Custom tab ('based upon the selection the administrator made in the Data Object list'), but the Validation page adds an object-specific rule the Custom page does not have: 'Field Validation: This will display the list of columns from the validation table.' So C's content is a validation-table column list, not an invoice field list, whenever B is Field Validation. C also fixes the data type that constrains column F.

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Column D, derived from the C selection. Two corpus notes attach here: 'If you use the In or Not In operators for Expense Types, you can select multiple check boxes to include as many expense types as are required', and the multi-value Any/Every rule. Severe constraint from validation-conditional-expressions-67302876.md: 'The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator. This is the same for the Detail Allocation object.'

sequence.action: choose Any or Every qualifier
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED on this page, unlike on the Custom tab: 'Some fields can have multiple values. When a field with multiple values is selected, the administrator must choose whether the condition will fire if Any or Every value matches.' Sits immediately after D because it qualifies the operator, and only appears for multi-value fields.

sequence.action: confirm or change auto-selected value
sequence.rationale: Column E. 'The system provides the option that best suits the previous choices. Change it if necessary' — auto-populated after D, so corpus-stated to sit here. Validation-only addition: 'List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists and is only available on the second data object selection list.' List Validation is therefore an E-only object and can never appear in column B. validation-conditional-expressions-67302876.md adds a second E-only restriction: 'The Detail Allocation data object can only be on the right-hand side of the expression.'

sequence.action: select from helper pane
sequence.rationale: Column F, and the tightest-constrained cell on the page. Three stated behaviours: 'List Validation: This will display all currently configured custom simple lists'; 'Field Validation: This will display the list of columns from the validation table. Only columns that match the data type selected in field C above will display.' The type-filter against C is explicit and has no Custom-tab equivalent.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column G: 'Select zero to three parentheses, depending on the complexity of the condition.' Same wording as the Custom editor; closes the row after F.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: Column H: 'Select either option to join the current condition to the next condition.' Meaningful only when another row follows. Validation rules are expected to be MULTI-condition by design, not by complexity: 'Each condition using the Field Validation data object narrows down the list of potential matches. To match an invoice/entry item field with a field in the validation table, it is necessary to use multiple conditions to specify the correct validation table row.' The Validation page does not restate Insert/Remove row controls — do not assume the Custom tab's insert_condition/remove_condition are the same controls here; the corpus is silent.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Next. The Actions page appears.' Second Next. This whole Actions step is unique to Validation and is what makes the wizard four steps.

sequence.action: select action type
sequence.rationale: POSITION FLAGGED, FIELD IS A PLACEHOLDER. The corpus step is 'Select the appropriate action' with three enumerated values — 'Field update only', 'Exception only', 'Update, then exception' (summary-the-basic-process-of-creating-validation-rules-7f36bed3.md renders the third as 'Field update, then exception'). No field id exists for this selector in the supplied set. It is load-bearing for ordering: the selection determines whether the field-update sub-page and the Exception page appear at all. It needs its own field, and its three values must not be folded into exception_visibility.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Next. If you selected a field update action, the Actions page refreshes with additional fields.' Third Next, and a CONDITIONAL branch — the From Data Source / From Field Name / To Data Source / To Field Name mapping fields appear only on the field-update branches. Those four fields are documented in add-a-validation-rule-0b31c4c0.md but have no ids in the supplied set; they are omitted rather than mapped onto unrelated ids.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: 'Select Next. If you selected an action including an exception, the Exception page appears.' Reached only on the Exception-bearing branches. Same three visibility values as the Custom tab, spelled here as 'Invoice Owner, Approver and Invoice Processor' (no comma before 'and') — a wording variance from the Custom tab's list, not a different set.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Choose from an existing exception or decide to create a new exception by first choosing from Exception Visibility' — the corpus explicitly puts visibility BEFORE the branch, which is why order 24 precedes this. Then 'Select New to open the New Exception window.'

sequence.action: type
sequence.rationale: Inside the New Exception window. The corpus says only 'Complete the appropriate fields' for the Validation path, so the code/level/text triple is carried over from the exception model documented for the Custom and Random paths — the field set is corpus-stated, the internal ordering is INFERRED.

sequence.action: set level
sequence.rationale: Determines whether the fired rule blocks submission: 'If there are exceptions generated that are above the exception level limit... then the invoice will not be submitted and will not enter the first step of a workflow.'

sequence.action: type
sequence.rationale: The message shown to the audience picked in order 24.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Save.' Closes the window and returns to the Exception page with the new exception selected.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'The exception you created is pre-selected. Select Done to include the exception with the validation rule and finish this task.' Corpus-stated terminal action — note Validation ends on Done, exactly like Custom, despite having one more wizard step.

configSteps.name: Build a Field Validation / List Validation lookup condition
configSteps.goal: Encode the constraint system that governs Validation-tab conditions when the Field Validation, List Validation or Detail Allocation data objects are in play — required columns, column ordering, operator restriction, side-of-expression restriction, and the short-code lookup behaviour for list, city, state/province and country fields.

sequence.action: select data object
sequence.rationale: Gate for the entire step and therefore first: 'The Field Validation data object must be selected in order to use fields in the validation table for comparison.' Until this is chosen in column B, none of the validation-table columns are reachable in C or F. Corpus-stated precondition, not inferred.

sequence.action: add condition on the Type column
sequence.rationale: Mandatory companion to order 1: 'The Type and Id 01 fields must be included when using the Field Validation data object.' Type comes before the Id columns because it is what disambiguates reused columns — 'The Type field in the validation table allows the client to reuse columns for different data. The type field is just one of the values that appear in the validation table.' The relative order of Type vs Id 01 is INFERRED from the sentence order; only their joint inclusion is stated.

sequence.action: add condition on Id 01
sequence.rationale: The second mandatory column. Named explicitly and separately from the higher Id columns because it is the anchor of the numeric-order rule in order 4.

sequence.action: add conditions on Id 02..Id n in order
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED ordering, one of the few hard sequence rules in this corpus: 'When using the Field Validation object the Id fields must all be used in numeric order 1 through n. For example, if you use Id 5 you must use Id 1 through Id 4 first.' Each added Id column narrows the match further — 'Each condition using the Field Validation data object narrows down the list of potential matches.'

sequence.action: restrict operator to equal
sequence.rationale: Applies to every condition created in orders 2-4, hence positioned after them: 'The only operator that can be used against the Id columns and the Type column is the equal operator. This is the same for the Detail Allocation object.' This overrides the general 'The list of operators will change depending on the type of data being compared' behaviour for these specific columns.

sequence.action: select validation-table column
sequence.rationale: With Field Validation selected in B, column C 'will display the list of columns from the validation table'. Sits here because it is the concrete cell the Type/Id conditions above are written into, and because the data type it fixes constrains order 8.

sequence.action: select right-hand data object
sequence.rationale: Column E, after the left-hand side is fully specified. Two E-only rules converge here: 'The Detail Allocation data object can only be on the right-hand side of the expression', and List Validation 'is only available on the second data object selection list'.

sequence.action: select matching column or list value
sequence.rationale: Column F, last cell of the row. Type-filtered by C — 'Only columns that match the data type selected in field C above will display' — so it cannot be chosen before order 6.

sequence.action: select Detail Allocation as the right-hand object
sequence.rationale: The list-type validation path, recorded after the Field Validation path because it is the alternative object: 'The Detail Allocation data object is used to validate invoice/line item fields against a list-type validation.' Bound by both the right-hand-side-only rule and the equal-operator-only rule above.

sequence.action: select List Validation as the right-hand object
sequence.rationale: Third object variant, available only in column E. Chosen at this point because selecting it is what triggers the helper pane in order 11.

sequence.action: select a configured simple list from the helper pane
sequence.rationale: Directly caused by order 10 — CORPUS-STATED cause and effect: 'When the List Validation object is selected, the List Validation Helper pane will appear on the right side of the page, displaying the configured simple lists.' Behaviour of the resulting comparison: 'When looking up list values, the list item short code is used', with three stated cases — copying between lists uses 'the source list short code for the current value... to look up the short code in the target list'; copying from a text field compares 'the text field value... to the short code value'; copying from a constant compares 'that value... to the short code value'.

sequence.action: reference the Entry City field
sequence.rationale: Field-specific lookup behaviour, grouped after the general list behaviour because it is a special case of it: 'When using the Entry City field in validations, the location code for the city is used. You must import the location codes into the validation table to validate the city values.' The import is a prerequisite outside the UI — flag it as a data dependency, not a click.

sequence.action: place the validation on the LEFT and State/Province on the RIGHT
sequence.rationale: The only field in this corpus with an explicit side-of-expression requirement, so its position in the row is dictated, not chosen: 'Validation conditions using this field must have the validation on the left side of the condition, and the State/Province field on the right side: Field_validation.ID_1 = Entry.State/Province.' Note this pins Field Validation to column B and Entry to column E — the reverse of the Detail Allocation rule. Uses 'the country sub code for the state/province', which must be imported first.

sequence.action: reference the Entry Country field
sequence.rationale: Third special-cased lookup field, same shape as City: 'the country code for the country is used. You must import the location country codes into the validation table to validate the country values.' No side restriction is stated for Country — do not extrapolate the State/Province rule onto it.

sequence.action: join the lookup conditions
sequence.rationale: Last, because it binds the completed rows into the single narrowing expression the corpus describes. The worked example is stated verbatim: 'The Account Code equals PMT validation table entry for Id 01 "Balance Sheet" AND Custom01 (Cost Center) on the allocation has a value entered (is not blank).' That example shows a Field Validation condition and a Detail Allocation condition joined by AND — the canonical shape of a lookup expression.

configSteps.name: Author a Random audit rule and set its numeric rate
configSteps.goal: Create a Random-tab rule inline in the grid, open the Rule Type window and enter the Percentage or Sequential numeric value with its documented maximum, then attach an exception, groups and event, save and activate.

sequence.action: select menu
sequence.rationale: access-random-audit-da5f6693.md step 1: 'Select Administration   Invoice.' Same entry point as the other two tabs.

sequence.action: select left-menu item
sequence.rationale: 'Select Audit Rules (left menu). The Audit Rules page appears.'

sequence.action: select tab
sequence.rationale: 'Select the Random tab.' Recorded against the Audit Rules navigation because no distinct field id for the tab exists in the supplied set. Unlike Custom and Validation, Random is consistently called a TAB across every page that references it.

sequence.action: click into the first grid row and type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED first authoring action, and structurally different from the other two tabs: there is no New/Create button and no wizard. 'Use the first line (yellow background) in the grid to add a new rule. Select in the Name field, and then enter the rule name.' Editing is inline in the grid, which is why the whole rule is committed by a single Save at order 12 rather than by Done.

sequence.action: click the Type field to open the Rule Type window
sequence.rationale: 'Select the Type field. The Rule Type window appears.' Corpus-stated as step 2 of the procedure, immediately after Name. The Type cell is a launcher, not an in-cell dropdown — the actual choice is made in a modal, which is why the numeric input in order 6/7 lives on a different page from the grid.

sequence.action: select Percentage and enter the percentage
sequence.rationale: THE NUMERIC INPUT THE PRIOR BUILD MISSED. 'Select either: Percentage and then enter the appropriate percentage.' Its bound is documented in random-audit-rules-8b29a270.md: 'The percentage audit is based on a percent of invoices submitted (for example 10%). Then, approximately 10% of the invoices submitted by the selected group or groups are selected randomly and audited. (The maximum is 100 %.)' Behavioural caveat worth carrying: 'The percentage-based random audit rule is based on averages. In the long term, the desired percentage of the invoices will be audited. In the short term, the exact percentage may be slightly more or less.' Mutually exclusive with order 7.

sequence.action: select Sequential and enter the count
sequence.rationale: The other branch of the same choice, occupying the SAME position as order 6, not a following action: 'Sequential and then enter the appropriate number.' Bound: 'The sequential audit is based on some number of invoices that users submit (for example, 10 invoices). Then, every 10th invoice submitted by the selected group or groups is audited. (The maximum is 999,999.)' Note the two branches have different maxima — 100 vs 999,999 — so the numeric constraint depends on the Type selection above it.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Save.' This Save closes the Rule Type modal only and is DISTINCT from the grid Save at order 12 — the corpus issues two Save instructions in one procedure. Conflating them loses the modal round-trip.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: 'In the Event field, select either: Payment Request Submit / Payment Post Request Submit.' Corpus-stated step 5, after the Rule Type modal closes. Only two values — far narrower than the Custom or Validation event lists, because a random rule can only sample at submit. random_audit_rule_event is the same control under an alternate id, not a second field.

sequence.action: click the Exception Code field to open the Exceptions window
sequence.rationale: 'Select the Exception Code field. The Exceptions window appears.' Same launcher pattern as the Type cell: a grid cell that opens a modal. Positioned after Event per the corpus's numbered steps.

sequence.action: select from dropdown
sequence.rationale: 'From the Exception Visibility list, select the users who are able to see the exception message.' Stated before the existing-vs-new exception choice, matching the Custom tab's ordering. Inside this window the corpus then branches: 'Using the exceptions list, you can: Use an existing exception. Create a new exception.' A new exception is built with new_exception / exception_code / exception_level / exception_text / save_exception exactly as on the Custom tab — summary-the-basic-process-of-creating-random-audit-rules-e794c09f.md confirms the triple: 'Selects (or creates) the appropriate exception, which includes: Exception code, Exception level, Exception text.'

sequence.action: select group configurations
sequence.rationale: 'In the Editable By field, select the group configuration(s) that can edit this rule.' Corpus-stated step 8 — AFTER the exception, which inverts the Custom tab's order (where groups precede conditions and exceptions). Do not normalise the two.

sequence.action: select group configurations
sequence.rationale: 'In the Applies To field, select the appropriate group configuration(s) to which this rule applies.' The summary page adds that the administrator 'Identifies the group to which the rule applies and whether or not the rule is inherited to the groups below it', but the Random procedure documents NO inherited toggle and no id exists for one — record the gap, do not borrow the Custom tab's control.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Save.' The second, grid-level Save — this is what commits the inline row. Random ends on Save, not Done; that difference from both other tabs is corpus-stated.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'With the rule selected, select Activate.' CORPUS-STATED as a separate step AFTER Save — the Random tab has no Active=Yes field in the create flow, so activation is a distinct post-save action, unlike Custom and Validation which activate via the Active dropdown inside the wizard. Constraint to enforce at this point: 'Your company should have only one active random audit rule for each group configuration. The system may let you activate more than one random rule, but the results will be unreliable.'

configSteps.name: View, modify, deactivate and remove an existing rule
configSteps.goal: Cover the list-level controls on all three tabs — the rule-name link and its two different view behaviours, Modify, Activate/Deactivate, and the two different destructive paths (checkbox + Delete Selected Rows on Custom; Remove, with confirmation on Validation).

sequence.action: click rule name link
sequence.rationale: NEW UI variant. view-a-custom-audit-rule-a4c909b3.md: 'On the Custom Rules tab, click the name of the rule you want to view.' First because viewing is non-destructive and is the entry point to the other lifecycle actions. rule_name_link is the same control under an unprefixed id, which exists in both a legacy and a new-UI form.

sequence.action: read panel
sequence.rationale: Immediate result of order 1 in the NEW UI: 'The Quick View panel appears on the right side of the page, showing the rule details and exception details.' A read-only side panel — no navigation, no Next, no Finish. This is the sharpest legacy/new divergence in the whole page.

sequence.action: click rule name link
sequence.rationale: LEGACY UI variant, occupying the SAME position as order 1 rather than following it. view-a-custom-audit-rule-45537e5c.md: 'On the Custom Audit Rule List page, select the name (link) of the rule you want to view. The Create New Custom Audit Rule page appears.' Note the legacy page name differs (Custom Audit Rule List vs Custom Rules) and the link opens the FULL WIZARD, not a panel.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: LEGACY ONLY. 'Select Next to move through the pages.' Viewing in the legacy UI means walking the same three wizard steps used for authoring — there is no read-only surface. Repeat per page.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: LEGACY ONLY, and the one place in this corpus where the wizard terminates on FINISH rather than Done: 'Select Finish when done.' The authoring and editing paths both end on Done; only the legacy view path ends on Finish. Do not normalise these into one button.

sequence.action: select rule row
sequence.rationale: Row selection is a stated prerequisite for Modify: 'On the Custom page, select the rule you want to edit. Select Modify. The Audit Rule step appears.' Recorded here against the Modify control because no separate row-select field id exists for the edit path (CustomRuleRowCheckbox is documented only for the delete path). modify_button is the same control under its unprefixed id. Both legacy and new-UI edit files (6b5ffce1, ebccc173) are byte-identical, so this action does not vary by variant.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Make any desired changes. Select Next. The Conditions step appears... Select Next. The Exception step appears.' Editing replays the authoring wizard in the same order, so all condition-editor columns from the custom-rule step apply unchanged here.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Select Done.' Terminal action of the edit path — matching the authoring path, and differing from the legacy VIEW path's Finish at order 5.

sequence.action: click rule name link then Modify
sequence.rationale: Validation's edit path is shaped differently and must not be copied from Custom: 'On the Validation tab, select the name (link) of the rule you want to change. Select Modify. Make the desired changes. Select Done.' The name LINK is the selector here (Custom selects the ROW), there is no documented Next-by-Next walk through the four steps, and it goes straight to Done.

sequence.action: select rule then click Activate or Deactivate
sequence.rationale: 'On the Custom tab, select the rule you want to affect. Choose Deactivate or Activate, whichever applies.' Two-action sequence collapsed onto one control because the corpus gives no separate selector field. Placed before the destructive actions because the corpus repeatedly frames it as the safer alternative: 'Instead of deleting a rule, you can deactivate it. This way, the rule is still available if you want to use it in the future.' deactivate_activate is the same control under its unprefixed id; both legacy and new-UI files are identical, so no variant split.

sequence.action: select rule then click Activate or Deactivate
sequence.rationale: 'On the Validation page, select the rule to activate or deactivate. Select Activate or Deactivate depending on the action you want to perform.' Same shape as Custom but note the label order is reversed in the corpus text (Activate first) and the page is called 'Validation page' here versus 'Validation tab' in the edit procedure.

sequence.action: select rule then click Deactivate or Activate
sequence.rationale: 'On the Random tab, select the desired rule. Select Deactivate or Activate, whichever applies.' Carries the extra Random-only constraint from the create flow — only one active random rule per group configuration should exist, so activating one here implies deactivating another.

sequence.action: select checkbox on the rule row
sequence.rationale: Deletion on the Custom tab is CHECKBOX-driven, not selection-driven: 'On the Custom Audit Rule List page, select the check box associated with the desired rule.' This is a different selection mechanic from Modify and Deactivate, which both say 'select the rule'. rule_row_checkbox is the same control under its unprefixed id. Both delete files (1ba67b2e, 5736c0e0) are identical, so this holds in both variants.

sequence.action: click button
sequence.rationale: 'Choose Delete Selected Rows.' Plural — the checkbox mechanic at order 13 exists precisely because this control acts on a multi-row selection. NO confirmation dialog is documented for the Custom path, which is a real asymmetry against Validation at order 16. delete_selected_rows is the same control under its unprefixed id.

sequence.action: select rule then click Remove
sequence.rationale: Validation deletes via a differently named, single-select control: 'On the Validation page, select the rule to delete. Select Remove.' Neither a checkbox nor 'Delete Selected Rows' appears on this tab. Guidance: 'Use this option only when you are certain the rule is no longer needed — deactivate it instead if you may want to reuse it later.'

sequence.action: click Yes in the confirmation
sequence.rationale: Mandatory second step on the Validation path only: 'The following confirmation message appears: Remove selected audit rule(s)? Select Yes to remove the audit rule from the list and the system.' Note the confirmation text says 'audit rule(s)' even on the Validation tab — record it verbatim rather than correcting it.

sequence.action: select rule then click Remove
sequence.rationale: Third destructive variant: 'On the Random tab, select the rule you want to remove. Select Remove.' Two steps only — no checkbox and NO confirmation is documented, unlike Validation. Warning: 'Once you have removed a rule, the system will permanently delete it. If you think you might want to use it again, deactivate it instead of removing it.'
